characters/companions.title: Companions
characters/companions.content:
Luna
Vander’s celestial companion: a silver cat with glowing golden markings and blue eyes, wearing a silver collar set with a blue moonstone. She found Vander lost in the woods after he was cast out, spoke into his mind, and set him on Selûne’s path. The church of Selûne named her. Since S25 she can grow into a towering, glowing, saddled mount (“is that a giant cat?”) and shrink back to a house cat at will. In S27 she gave Laura a blessing for her journey, and Leon Thrace stroked her whiskers (“for generations cats have protected this noble house”).
In S29 she healed Kaelith and carried her and Osric out of the dungeon. Luna vanished after Selûne’s rebuke of Vander, dropping both passengers. She returned in S31, when a voice told Vander “all has been restored” after the rope-works explosion. She is with him at the Green Leaf. See Session 29 and Session 31.
Ariane
Odettia’s owl familiar. Aerdrie Faenya sends Odettia visions through her. In S26 she scouted the woods and saw pale women stalking a lone traveller. In S28 she and Barry searched opposite stretches of coast; the owls saw no cliff activity. Ariane also showed Odettia a distant winged silhouette. Odettia wondered if it was a griffon, but its identity was not confirmed.
In S29 she guided the escaping boy Brennan, helped establish the warehouse escape route and alerted Milo at the Green Leaf.
Barry
Kaelith’s owl familiar since S26, “a happy chappy”. His night scouting confirmed the coven at Harlan’s farm. In S28 he joined Ariane in searching the coast while the party investigated the chapel.
Milo Bramble
See Milo Bramble.
The watchtower griffon
In S30, Odettia’s warming Griffontack and her call brought down the same griffon that touched her amulet at the watchtower in the Fields of the Dead. She felt an immediate connection when she touched it. The creature agreed to help temporarily, discussed as until midnight. Odettia and Kaelith mounted it for a planned manor raid; play paused before the raid. It is a willing partnership, with no permanent ownership established. See Session 30.
Biscuit
Befriended during Reza Sahil’s contests (S18).
The owls and the raid (S31)
Ariane scouted Leon and the medic in the greenhouse; Barry returned from the cliff after Kaelith contacted him. Later Barry spotted the search force moving in the griffon’s flight direction. His attempted warning through Ariane reached Odettia only as “dungeon, urgent,” reversing its intended meaning and prompting fear for her friends underground.
The griffon carried the raiders through the conservatory and brought Leon and the medic back to the farm. Its ice breath came from Odettia’s temporary Dragon’s Breath spell. It keeps the medic under Suggestion pinned at the pause; no permanent power or ownership was established. See Session 31.
The midnight parting (S32)
Luna carried Vander around the troops and helped him collect Kaelith. Vander cast Zone of Truth through her during the interrogation. Barry scouted the Green Leaf and later watched Leon from the trees. At midnight Leon looked directly at Barry, and Kaelith lost the familiar link. Ariane was sent to investigate an unidentified figure on the coast. The watchtower griffon landed to let Odettia dismount at midnight, accepted her thanks and flew away. See Session 32.

characters/kaelith.title: Kaelith Autumn-Born
characters/kaelith.content:
Elf druid (Circle of the Land) · 110 years old · out of her own time
Who she is
Born in the eladrin city of Cendriane in the Feywild, in the last days of the war between the eladrin and the drow. Her parents, Elrond Celeborn and Vaelora Oakheart, were the city’s wizard-protectors and the king’s right hand. As the end came, they cast a spell on her. She woke somewhere, and some time, unknown.
Her name means “Arcane Spirit of the Living Forest”. She loves forests, tea, food, sleep, animals and spellbooks. She struggles with social cues, procrastinates, and is always late. She dislikes arrogance, will break laws to protect the weak, and distrusts drow by instinct while knowing today’s drow are not the ones she fought. Her prized possession is her mother’s emerald jewellery.
When she tried to go home, she found Cendriane fallen long ago and overrun by the undead of a vampire lord, Kannoth. She barely escaped. She is looking for her people’s descendants, and for a way to rework her parents’ spell and save her city.
The fading
Her parents’ spell is coming undone, and her body is starting to fade out of the present:

S13: A dream left her hand translucent for three heartbeats.
S16: In the storm the fading climbed to her forearm, until an emerald she had bought in Baldur’s Gate crumbled to dust and it stopped.
S25: Near Yara’s preservation magic she felt solid for the first time in this age. Then she met Corv, fading for five years from a different cause, and understood she faces the same slow disappearance.
S27: At midnight in the manor her hand faded again.
S30: Her left hand and forearm vanished up to the elbow and did not return. Odettia’s Identify named the failing spell Temporal Refuge: its deterioration tears her body apart, rather than taking her home. A taste of Corv’s unfinished remedy had no effect, and her bear form had only three legs. See Session 30.

Along the way


S8: Zivra’s prophecy.


S10: Found a crossing point toward Cendriane in eladrin ruins.


S13: Secretly followed Odettia into a Black Boars fight and was nearly killed.


S12 onward: Recognised Captain Neve Saren’s emerald necklace as Cendriane work. During the storm (S16), Neve’s necklace grew warm as Kaelith faded.


S24: Fought the storehouse guardian with Vander.


S25: A day at Yara’s apothecary. Invented “Antivomix”, cured a sick boy (“Kaelith the Wise”), and struck a deal with Corv for his unfinished cure. Healed Laura’s hidden bruises.


S26: New owl Barry scouted the coven. She charmed Osric into honesty and read the age of the bones in the lair.


S27: Questioned Laura with Vander. At midnight Corv’s vial pointed down, beneath the manor, toward the missing ingredient.


S28: Scouted the chapel and dungeon as a ladybird, located Osric in a cart, and saw prisoners connected to smoky tendrils beneath a closed door. Cast Spike Growth and Land’s Aid, then severed one tendril with Produce Flame. Crossbow bolts reduced her to 3 hit points and broke her concentration; Vander healed her to 23 before play paused mid-fight. No ingredient for Corv’s cure has been recovered.


S29: Used Flaming Sphere to sever the prisoners’ tendrils and burned through cell locks. Her ritual detected a mage using ice magic beyond the reinforced door, which resisted her fire; Corv’s ingredient remains unrecovered. Odettia knocked her unconscious to enable the retreat, and Vander carried her out on Luna. She woke when Luna vanished, healed herself and reached Harlan’s farmhouse. See Session 29.


S30: Still intended to finish the remedy for Corv first and learn to make another. Her Pot of Awakening began to stir but was not fully awakened. Heard Osric’s account alongside Vander, used Elementalism after Milo’s explosion, and mounted the griffon with Odettia for a planned manor raid and ladybird infiltration. The dungeon return has not yet happened.


Kit
Mother’s emerald jewellery · a river stone from the eladrin ruins · Corv’s vial · lumen leaves · owl familiar Barry
Session 31
Kaelith burned the greenhouse’s Lily of the Shade plants and infiltrated the manor as a ladybird. She found the “cuttings” ledger, a receipt for a live specimen and accompanying specialist, and Leon’s undated night observation chart. Beyond the scrubbed cells she found restraint chairs, heard of a prisoner transfer in two days, and followed sulphurous pipes to Leon’s bedroom. The vial stayed dormant: its former target was absent. She rejoined Vander, Osric and Milo at the Green Leaf, despairing over the lost lead and her missing forearm. Her attempted owl warning became “dungeon, urgent” to Odettia. No ingredient or cure was obtained. See Session 31.
Session 32
Corv faded before her and left the word “Oblex.” Kaelith took the second vial Vander found, sought Leon and helped hide the party’s trail using Elementalism. At midnight her vial reacted in Leon’s direction. She lost her link to Barry when the figure looked up at him. Kaelith used Blur and began retreating after a voice in the shadows let her go. See Session 32.

characters/odettia.title: Odettia D'Ilithrea Belabranta
characters/odettia.content:
Aasimar sorcerer (Draconic Sorcery) · Waterdeep noble in flight · chosen of Aerdrie Faenya
Who she is
The only child of Wilhelm and Aubri Belabranta, a noble Waterdeep family that breeds griffons. She was born aasimar to human parents. She grew up on the family’s country estate south of the Forlorn Hills, riding griffons, studying, and sneaking off to play cards in the tavern at Secomber.
She is six feet tall, with wavy white hair, a long feather sweeping back from above her ears, bright orange eyes with black markings, and a swan-like white dress. People can never tell whether the feathers are fashion or part of her.
Her ancestor Ilithrea Belabranta slew the green dragon Elaacrimalicros and earned the friendship of the Aarakocra and the Avariel of the Star Mounts. Her draconic magic comes from that line.
Why she ran

Since birth she had been promised to Deryc Gundwynd of the hippogriff-breeding Gundwynds, a family connected to the Black Boars gang. On the night before her wedding, an avoral messenger of Aerdrie Faenya came to her balcony: “You are not meant to be caged.” At its touch her magic woke. She left that night with her pack and the family amulet, the Griffontack of Belabranta.
Along the way


S8: Zivra’s prophecy.


S9: The Griffontack awoke at a watchtower.


S11: In Baldur’s Gate, the family steward Theron Vale was offering a 500 gp reward for her. She confronted him in disguise.


S13–14: She fought Black Boars in a tavern, and later watched them threaten Theron.


S15: She freed Milo’s mother from a Guild debt, signing as “Morgan Duskbane”.


During the voyage: She attuned a hat of disguise and bonded the owl Ariane, through whom Aerdrie Faenya sends visions; one showed a frightened ruler of Amn and a closing golden cage. Her wings became known to all.


S24: In Saltmere she disguised herself, slipped into the old governor’s funeral through the priest’s entrance, and ended up running the service. She drew close to the young governor, Leon Thrace. Later she saw his eyes flash crimson.


S25: A letter from her parents reached her in Saltmere. At the Tailored Needle she found a gift for needlework. A pair of velvet gloves brought a vision of the murdered governess through Isolde’s eyes, and she promised Henrietta the truth.


S26: She grappled the coven’s leader to stop the fighting and was bitten. She resisted the charm and found the tapestry of the two crowned women.


S27: The bite is spreading slowly. She has about three days for a cure (see open-threads). She sat beside Leon at dinner, sent Isolde word that Henrietta still waits for her, and secretly placed a Clairvoyance sensor on Leon’s desk.


S28: Heard orders about the dead vampire through Clairvoyance. Identify on Milo drew a possessive voice and burned her hand. Helped examine Sibbet and Hobb, impersonated a guard to infiltrate the dungeon with Vander as her supposed prisoner, and used Command in the ensuing fight. Her bite remains uncured.


S29: Covered the dungeon rescue with Fog Cloud, healed Osric and melted three locks with phoenix fire. Questioned the escapees behind an illusory wall, recognised the Gundwynd crest on Osric’s shipping container and found his charge sheet. Knocked Kaelith unconscious with her dagger handle so the party could retreat, then flew out. Guided Brennan toward the Green Leaf, alerted Milo and left a warning on the farmhouse’s warded door. See Session 29.


S30: Identified Kaelith’s failing Temporal Refuge and the poison affecting Osric. With Quinn, heard Isolde’s account of Celandine and Leon and promised a meeting at dusk. Isolde willingly released her bond, but the item and priest’s cleansing are still needed. Called the watchtower griffon through the warming Griffontack and mounted it with Kaelith for a planned raid on the manor. See Session 30.


Kit
Griffontack · hat of disguise · owl familiar Ariane
Session 31
Odettia led the griffon raid, using Ariane to find Leon and the medic, cold Dragon’s Breath to breach the greenhouse and Suggestion to prevent the medic using magic against her allies. She brought both men to Harlan’s farm. She showed Leon the cellar tapestry and challenged his account of his family; he admitted knowing his vampiric parentage and agreed to speak to Isolde, without explaining his cure. A garbled owl message left her fearing her friends needed rescue in the dungeon. She remains at the farm as Isolde approaches; her cleansing is still unperformed. See Session 31.
Session 32
Odettia challenged Leon over the prisoners and knocked him and the medic unconscious as the troops approached. She brought the medic to the coven’s caves, questioned him and offered safe passage. When Leon warned of the midnight takeover, she set him down safely in remote woodland. The griffon departed at midnight. Odettia sent Ariane after sighting a figure on the coast. She has about twenty-four hours left for cleansing. See Session 32.

characters/quinn.title: Quinn McKenzie-Talen
characters/quinn.content:
Dhampir rogue · “traveller and beast hunter”
Who he is
Tall, lean and pale, with grey eyes ringed in crimson and slightly long canines that show only when he smiles, which is rarely. He dresses plainly under a dark cloak and makes himself forgettable on purpose.
His parents died in a war against the Dalki when he was a child. A vampire family, the McKenzies, adopted him and raised him at the edge of their settlement on rationed artificial blood and strict discipline. He will not feed on thinking creatures. He lives on artificial blood and Dalki blood, which he carries in a special flask.
From an old book he taught himself a shadow technique (he calls it the Punisher ability), once the craft of a family that kept order in the settlement. He travels after rumours of the Talen family, the other half of his name. Too poor to pay passage and unwilling to explain himself, he stowed away on the Maris.
Along the way


S18: Found in the hold of the Maris and, after some friction, became part of the crew. Lifted Reza Sahil’s map unnoticed.


S21: At the Viledel lighthouse he looked into the lighthouse orb and was knocked senseless. Since then an Orb Curse threatens to hand his body to the dread wraith’s spirit.


S24: With Milo he climbed the manor wall in borrowed priest’s robes, found the young lord’s shackled sickroom, and used his truesight to find the hidden stair to the dungeon.


S25: Heard of Brennick, a hunter bearing his book’s mark (two crossed lines through a closed eye) who went up the manor road decades ago and never came back. Built the Leon-as-vampire theory. At the docks he tasted blood in a “wine” bottle, read a restrained vampire’s bite on a drowned body, and stole Cole’s mortality register and governess notes.


S26: Fought the coven from the shadows, found the lair under the farm and the tapestry, and set up a private meeting with the coven’s leader.


S27:

Rolled a natural 20 against his curse.
Linked the party’s minds for the dinner.
Slipped out and found Celandine’s last letter hidden in a second tapestry.
Met Isolde in the orchard and bargained with her for Odettia’s release. He kept the letter until S30.



S28: Picked the chapel’s rear lock and helped uncover contradictions in the report on Sibbet and Hobb. Took Sibbet’s bracelet for Isolde. Distracted the cave guards with a drunken act, then followed the prisoner cart along the ceiling. Struck a dungeon guard with psychic blades and hid again; the fight is unfinished.


He has told the party his father was a vampire and his mother human.


S29: Killed a dungeon guard with psychic blades, picked cell locks and helped Odettia question the escapees. Found a ventilation opening and reported four people and unidentified mist beyond the reinforced door. During the retreat he stole twenty gold from a patrol guard. At Harlan’s farmhouse he smelled blood toward the cellar but postponed investigating. See Session 29.


S30: Resisted the orb curse again. Gave Sibbet’s bracelet and Celandine’s letter to Isolde, who called him brother. With Odettia, heard her account of the sisters, Leon’s illness and the blood shipments, and promised to arrange a meeting with Leon at dusk. Proposed a psychic link for the planned manor raid; its activation has not yet been established. See Session 30.


Kit
Two daggers · blood flask · a stolen map and stolen ledgers. Celandine’s letter and Sibbet’s bracelet were given to Isolde in S30.
Session 31
His attempt to extend the psychic link failed, leaving the separated groups without it. Quinn crossed the town wall and asked Yara about the orb curse; she warned of possible body/spirit separation, advised a soul-magic specialist and supplied three doses of temporary resistance aid. He bought Poison of Silence for fifty gold, then suffered a burned wrist during an unsuccessful pickpocket attempt. Back at the farm, he questioned Leon alongside Odettia. At dusk he and Isolde mingled blood in a mutual-aid bond, and she pledged her coven’s help when needed. They approached Leon, but the meeting itself has not yet been played. See Session 31.
Session 32
Quinn brought Isolde to meet Leon. Two coven members tried to enlist him in a hunt and offered blood. He felt Isolde’s direction through their bond and used a psychic link during the escape. At midnight he reached for Leon mentally, heard a changed voice and was cut off. See Session 32.

characters/vander.title: Vander Duskbane
characters/vander.content:
Human paladin (Oath of Devotion), sworn to Selûne · age 29 · goes by “Van” or “V”
Who he is
A big, red-bearded, golden-eyed Duskbane: 6′2″, kind, quick to trust, slow to anger, and remarkable when roused. He plays flute and harp and tells a good tavern story. He fears snakes, the dark overcoming the land, and dying before he has put things right.
He was raised by the Order of Aster at the Spires of the Morning in Waterdeep, training alongside his twin sister Morgan and older brother Sundar. Both outshone him, and he was given guard duty and the standard. He never knew his mother. His father Umber, a mighty paladin of Lathander, was found dead outside Waterdeep, gripping a golden key with a fire opal. The seven knights who rode with him were never found. Sundar left on an oath of vengeance.
The fall and the moon
At 27, two charming strangers drank with Vander and drew out everything he knew about the Order. The next morning a guard was dead and the key was gone from the reliquary. The Order cast him out, with Morgan leading the call.
Lost in the woods, he met Luna, a celestial silver cat, who told him his soul belongs to the Moonmaiden, “like his mother’s before him”. He swore himself to Selûne and trained with her church in Waterdeep, where he heard rumours that followers of Shar were behind the theft.
Along the way


S8: Zivra’s prophecy about his brother.


S11: Delivered Aldren Thace’s letter to Brother Callum at the Shrine of the Moonmaiden in Baldur’s Gate.


S13: At the Closed Door, learned that Sundar sold the key, through an agent calling himself “Mourne”. Set the stew record at the Lizard’s Cradle (8 bowls).


S18: Gained the greatsword Marianne.


S24: Fought the storehouse guardian with Kaelith.


S25: Luna’s first mount form. At Harlan’s farm he destroyed the risen farmer, buried him in the Order’s custom, found the Order’s symbol in the treeline and heard a four-note whistle he half-remembers.


S26: Saved Osric, one of his father’s seven, and chose to knock out the coven’s leader rather than kill her. Osric told him Sundar has turned to Shar and is hunting the rest of Umber’s company.


S27: Bought Laura’s story with gold and gave her Selûne’s blessing for the road. Ate a great deal at the governor’s table.


S28: Distracted chapel guards with rum, then posed as a prisoner to reach Osric in a guarded cart. Broke his bonds and fought in the dungeon. A missed swing strained his right shoulder (disadvantage on Strength saving throws until treated; healing spells alone do not fix it). Ended the session beside Kaelith after restoring 20 hit points with Lay on Hands; combat continues.


S29: Selûne let him see through Odettia’s fog, and he killed a guard. Found a key, thirty gold and Halflin’s charge sheet, which he retains. Carried Osric and the unconscious Kaelith out on Luna and bluffed past a patrol. After Selûne rebuked him for releasing people who prey on the weak, Luna vanished and his weapon blessing failed. Learned spells remain available. He intends to make amends; his shoulder still needs treatment. See Session 29.


S30: Used Lay on Hands to remove Osric’s poison. Heard his account of Umber’s WSS-cloaked killers, the key’s reported suppression of oblex copies and Sundar’s attack on the surviving knights. The key had been returned to the Order before the later reliquary theft. Vander intended to approach the manor by land while Odettia and Kaelith flew. Halflin remains at large; Luna and the weapon blessing remain lost, and his shoulder is untreated. See Session 30.


Kit
Marianne (greatsword; his old one was “Annabelle”) · trident · chain mail · holy symbol of Selûne (a blue eye ringed by seven stars) · Luna
Session 31
Vander felt an unexplained familiar hum after a strong Sunbolt, then entered Saltmere under a hood with Osric and Milo. A hooded guide calling herself Julianne sold him a lead to Halflin. He pursued the fugitive through the rope works, where Milo’s trap apparently killed Halflin. A voice announced “all has been restored,” and Luna returned; his divine blessing was restored. Pursued by guards, he fled with Osric and Milo to Gerta’s back room at the Green Leaf, where Kaelith joined them. His shoulder was not shown receiving treatment. See Session 31.
Session 32
Vander urged Milo to learn control, found Corv’s second vial and rode Luna around the search force. He cleared up the owl warning and doubled back for Kaelith. In the caves he cast Zone of Truth through Luna and freed the medic once the man identified the key’s location. He left the key with Leon after Leon’s warning. See Session 32.

index.title: Legends Among Gods, Monsters and Kings
index.content:
Kaelith, Odettia, Vander and Quinn above Saltmere, with Barry, Ariane and Luna.
Legends Among Gods, Monsters and Kings (MALKG) is a D&D 5e (2024) campaign on the Sword Coast and in the Moonshae Isles. The party is level 5. Thirty-two sessions have been played, from Daggerford to the midnight crisis in Saltmere.


                  
                  Draft 
                  
                

This wiki is a first draft built from the DM’s campaign records and session recordings. If something looks wrong, tell the DM.


The party






























Odettia D’Ilithrea BelabrantaAasimar sorcererRunaway Waterdeep noble, chosen of Aerdrie FaenyaVander DuskbaneHuman paladin of SelûneCast out of the Order of Aster; travels with the celestial cat LunaKaelith Autumn-BornElf druidSent forward in time from fallen Cendriane, and slowly fadingQuinn McKenzie-TalenDhampir rogueHunter raised by vampires, following his family’s trail
Travelling with them: Milo Bramble, plus Luna, Ariane and Barry.
Where things stand (after Session 32)
The oblex took control of Leon at midnight. Odettia left him in the woods wearing the Order of Aster key, and her griffon departed when its bargain ended. Kaelith’s vial reacted and her link to Barry went silent. The manor medic identified the Waterdeep Scientific Society and its reach before fleeing. Odettia sent Ariane to look at an unidentified figure on the coast. Read Session 32 · Open threads.

items.title: Items
items.content:
Griffontack of Belabranta

Odettia’s family amulet, which she took the night she fled. It awoke at the watchtower (S9). In S30 it grew warm as she sought the griffon; her call brought the same creature that had touched it at the watchtower. Touching the griffon gave her an immediate connection and its temporary help, discussed as lasting until midnight. Its wider powers remain unexplored. See the griffon and Session 30.
Marianne
Vander’s greatsword, won from Ser Callum Voss, a paladin of vengeance, in Odettia’s card game during Reza Sahil’s contests (S18). The blade bears a bloodthirsty etching. Vander’s previous greatsword was called “Annabelle”.
The Order of Aster key
A golden key with a fire opal, holy to Lathander. See The Order of Aster.
Corv’s vial
A vial of dark, bubbling liquid: Corv’s nearly finished cure, given to Kaelith (S25). It needs one last ingredient, “the thing that consumes”, and reacts when it is near. At midnight in the manor (S27) its contents pooled downward. In S29 the contents strained toward the reinforced dungeon door. In S31 Kaelith entered the room beyond it, but the vial was dormant and its former target absent. The missing ingredient was still unrecovered at the end of Session 31.
Celandine’s letter
Found by Quinn hidden in the manor’s tapestry (S27): “He knows. Keep the boy safe if I can’t. Love, your sister.” Quinn gave it to Isolde in S30. She wept as she read it, kept it and willingly released Odettia’s bond. The cleansing rite remains outstanding.
Sibbet’s bracelet
A metal, vine-like bracelet taken by Quinn from Sibbet’s right wrist in the chapel’s medical room (S28). He gave it to Isolde in S30 as a remembrance; she called it a kindness she would not forget. No magical properties have been established.
Others

Pot of Awakening: Kaelith’s shrub made a sound and the pot developed cracks in S30, but it was not yet fully awakened.
Hat of disguise: Odettia’s, attuned during the voyage.
Cap of water breathing: from the drowned wreck (S19).
Ship’s log: from the wreck. It records a Waterdeep navy mission to the Moonshaes about fifteen years ago.
Spiderweb coins: left by the sahuagin raiders (S17). They grow warm near the wreck.
Cole’s mortality register and governess notes: taken by Quinn (S25).
The storehouse cart ledger: taken by Vander (S24).
The tapestry of two crowned women: left in the coven’s lair. A second, named copy hangs in the manor.
A travel bag hidden with Celandine’s letter: 100 gp and survival tools.
Kaelith’s mother’s emerald jewellery, and a river stone from the eladrin ruins.
Thalwick’s book, bought in Baldur’s Gate (S15).
A replacement chart, won from Reza Sahil (S18).

Halflin’s charge sheet
Found by Vander on a dead dungeon guard in S29, alongside a cell key and thirty gold split between the two bodies. The sheet concerns Halflin, an elf and one of the twins released from the cells. It lists numerous alleged offences and an extraction scheduled for that day. Vander retains it. In S31 he pursued Halflin to the rope works, where Milo’s trap apparently killed the fugitive; no body was examined. The allegations on the sheet are not all independently established. See Session 29 and Session 31.
Yara’s resistance mixture
An amber bottle given to Quinn in S31: three doses, each granting advantage on his next orb-resistance check within twenty-four hours. It is an experimental aid using herbs and preservation magic, not a cure. No dose was used during the session. See Yara Dunwell.
Poison of Silence
Bought by Quinn from Yara for fifty gold in S31. Enough for roughly five arrows, described as interfering with a target’s magic. Precise saves, duration and other effects were deferred until use; it was not used during the session. See Session 31.
Manor records seen in S31
Kaelith read but did not take these records during her ladybird infiltration:

Greenhouse ledger: unfamiliar names, dates spanning five years and tally marks headed “cuttings.”
Study receipt: dated two weeks earlier; “live specimen” and “accompanying specialist.” It recorded receipt of goods rather than a price.
Medical observation chart: undated, for L. Thrace, normal daytime readings followed at 12:30 a.m. by “agitated,” “violent,” “new powers?”

Their full significance remains unresolved. See Session 31.
The vials and the griffon’s bargain (S32)
Corv left a second vial sewn into his robes. It looked like the first and gave off no detectable magic when Kaelith took it. At midnight, Kaelith’s vial shook and pooled towards Leon. Neither vial has been filled with a sample during play.
The griffon’s promise ended at midnight. It put Odettia down safely, bowed and departed. See Session 32.

lore/gods.title: Gods
lore/gods.content:
Selûne, the Moonmaiden: goddess of the moon and of travellers. Vander swore himself to her after Luna found him. Her holy symbol is a blue eye ringed by seven stars. The party has seen no sign of her worship on Saltmere.
Lathander, the Morninglord: patron of the Order of Aster and of Vander’s father Umber.
Shar, the Lady of Loss: Selûne’s eternal enemy. Her followers are rumoured to have stolen the key, and Osric says Sundar now serves her.
Aerdrie Faenya: goddess of wind and sky, of the Avariel. She freed Odettia (“You are not meant to be caged”), sends her visions through her owl Ariane, and gave her the vision of the murdered governess.
Sune: with Lathander, a traditional patron of the Duskbane family.

lore/oblexes-and-the-wss.title: Oblexes and the WSS
lore/oblexes-and-the-wss.content:
Oblexes

An oblex is an ooze that feeds on memories and can wear the shape of the people it consumes. The party met one in Bearbarrow (S6–7). It escaped from Priya’s cargo and replaced the stable hand Julius, and the party exposed it. That one was small and feral. Fire troubles them.
The WSS
The initials stamped on the strongbox in Priya’s wagon. The party has learned (from Cassia’s briefing in S10, and since):

The WSS is a Waterdeep group behind the oblex specimens.
A second specimen was shipped to Baldur’s Gate under the WSS mark. The strongbox itself was stolen during a drake ambush.
Their operative in Baldur’s Gate goes by Aldric Mourne. Cassia narrowed him to four men, including the brothers Erstin and Renard Holloway.
A ship, the Tideworth, left Baldur’s Gate shortly before the party arrived, heading west toward the Moonshaes. It carried a specimen, and the stolen Order of Aster key.

In Saltmere


Cole’s ledger shows a large payment to the Tideworth two weeks before the party arrived, marked “agent”. The party believes the ship delivered something to the manor.


Leon told the party the Tideworth docked about a week before the dinner. He offered to share what he knows about its cargo if they help him.


The dungeon (S28): about fifteen prisoners were connected to black, smoky tendrils running beneath a closed door. Some could not remember their own name or their mother’s name. Kaelith thought the strands reminiscent of the Bearbarrow creature, but more ethereal and less like ooze. Her Produce Flame severed one, and its detached end disintegrated. The prisoner showed no immediate change. At the time, the door was unopened and the source unidentified.


The party’s theories
At the end of S27, Kaelith wondered aloud whether Leon could be an oblex. Odettia thought him nothing like the Bearbarrow creature: he holds family memories, doesn’t flicker, and isn’t afraid of flame. Vander pointed out that oblexes steal memories. Nothing is settled.
New testimony (S30)
Osric described Umber’s killers wearing blue cloaks with gold WSS letters. He recalled records saying the Order of Aster key suppresses an oblex’s production of copies. That reported property has not been tested by the party.
Isolde said Leon had inherited vampiric blood, endured years of failed treatments and then abruptly recovered around his father’s death. She now smells sulphur on him and doubts he is her nephew. The party explained oblexes to her. Leon’s present condition and the source beyond the dungeon door remain unresolved. See Session 30.
The manor search (S31)
Kaelith saw a receipt dated two weeks earlier for a “live specimen” and an “accompanying specialist,” a ledger tallying “cuttings” across five years, and an undated medical chart describing Leon as “agitated,” “violent,” “new powers?” at 12:30 a.m. Beyond the cleaned cells were restraint chairs beneath pipes that led to Leon’s bedroom, with sulphurous residue inside. Staff expected another prisoner transfer in two days.
Leon admitted knowing his vampiric parentage and said a cure had been found. He recognised Odettia’s reference to an oblex, but did not explain the cure or the creature’s role. These new observations do not settle the party’s theories. See Session 31.
The medic’s testimony (S32)
Under Vander’s Zone of Truth, the manor medic identified the WSS as the Waterdeep Scientific Society and admitted membership. Its main laboratory is in Waterdeep, with the precise site still unknown. He reported two other oblex samples besides the one delivered to Saltmere. Their locations are unknown. He said his superiors wanted the ability to replace people for Waterdeep’s ruling class. Renard Holloway, whom he identified as Aldric Mourne, was a senior member and had left with the delivery ship as far as he knew.
He said the dungeon tendrils came from Leon. In his experience this was the first willing pact between an oblex and its host, and he suspected their souls had melded. He warned that starving the oblex might harm Leon and was unsure what separation would do. He also described a specialised magical flame and said the Society had copied the key’s suppression of replicas into other objects, with some failing in transit. These claims came from the medic. At midnight Quinn heard a changed voice before losing the psychic link, and Kaelith’s vial reacted from a distance. See Session 32.

lore/order-of-aster.title: The Order of Aster and the Key
lore/order-of-aster.content:
A martial order of Lathander based at the Spires of the Morning in Waterdeep, home to generations of Duskbane paladins and fighters. It raised Vander, his twin Morgan and his brother Sundar, and cast Vander out after the key was stolen.
Burial custom: a lantern is laid at the head of the grave before the body is lowered. Vander did this for Harlan.
The key
A holy relic of Lathander: a golden key with a fire opal set in its base. Vander’s father Umber died retrieving it. He was found outside Waterdeep still gripping it, and the seven knights who rode with him were never found.
How it moved:

It was stolen from the Order’s reliquary the morning after two strangers drew the Order’s secrets out of Vander in a tavern.
It was sold through Orin Castellar of the Closed Door by Sundar himself, about eight months before the party learned of it (S13). The buyer’s agent called himself “Mourne”.
It was collected by the Tideworth at the Baldur’s Gate docks.
It was seen by Osric around Leon Thrace’s neck at the old governor’s funeral in Saltmere (S24, told to the party in S26). At the S27 dinner, a chain around Leon’s neck disappeared beneath his shirt.

In S30, Osric recalled records saying the key suppressed an oblex’s ability to produce copies. The party has not tested that effect. He also explained that a member of Umber’s company returned the key to the Order after the fatal ambush, before the later reliquary theft. See Session 30.
In Saltmere
The Order’s symbol is carved into a tree in the woods by Harlan’s farm. A four-note whistle answered Vander there (S25). Osric, one of Umber’s seven, is on the island.
Still with Leon (S32)
The medic said the WSS copied the key’s suppression of oblex replicas into other objects, some of which failed in transit. He identified the key as still around Leon’s neck. Leon warned that removing it would make things worse, and the party left it with him. See Session 32.

lore/prophecies.title: Zivra's Prophecies
lore/prophecies.content:
Delivered by Madame Zivra in her tent at the carnival on the road south (S8).
Kaelith

The way back exists. The spell can be recast. The city can be joined once more. But the thread that carries you home must be cut from someone who has never seen its walls. One who will walk beside you, whose roots drink from the same soil as yours though they have never seen its trees. The weave will ask for them. It will not return what it takes. You will carry the cost of this blood back to a city that will never know what was paid.

Odettia

The wind that freed you will ask you to be its blade. There is a cage. Thousands behind it. Trapped by it. The one who holds it shut is not cruel, not wicked, only afraid. The lock will only answer to an end. The wind will show you the door and call it mercy. It will call it freedom. It will wait for you to decide what to call it and if you will remain its chosen.

Later, through her owl Ariane, Aerdrie Faenya showed Odettia a vision: a frightened ruler of Amn, and a golden cage closing.
Vander

Your brother kneels to a God, but not the one you think. He went looking for the ones who killed your father. He found them. They did not fight him. They opened a door your father died to keep shut. And your brother, who was always the strongest of you, walked through it. When you find him, and you will, he will ask you to walk through it with him. He will mean it. He will love you when he asks.

In S26 Osric told Vander that Sundar has turned to Shar.

lore/the-farm-coven.title: The Farm Coven
lore/the-farm-coven.content:
A coven of vampires that has lived beneath Harlan’s farm outside Saltmere for twelve years. It is led by Isolde, an older, calm woman, with at least three younger, pale companions.
What the party knows

How they came: frightened and running from “something in the manor house”. Laura hid them in her cellar and kept their arrangement for twelve years. They fed on animals and on weekly bottled blood shipped from the harbour as “wine”, in carts bearing the governor’s symbol. They promised to leave humans alone, and Harlan never knew.
The lair (found S26): hundreds of empty blood bottles; a tapestry of two crowned women, the only thing Isolde brought with her; animal bones one to ten years old.
How they feed: with restraint and elegance. Two neat punctures in the crook of the elbow, the body drained, no struggle.
Why they turned: the harbour blood stopped a week or two before S27. Since then the coven has gone feral and hunts openly. Leon counts eight townspeople dead, including his captain of the guard. On Leon’s first day as governor, the coven returned his negotiator’s head.
Harlan: killed by Isolde when Laura said yes to “Do you want me to take care of this?” after he beat her.
Their enemy: “a greater evil” in the manor that “wears a familiar face in town”. Isolde says “they killed my sister in front of me” and holds everyone in the manor complicit.
The truce: after Vander spared Isolde (S26), she offered a guarded truce. In S27 she asked Quinn to let her into the manor and offered to release Odettia’s bite in exchange for her sister’s letter.
Losses: in S28 the party identified the dead vampire as Sibbet, whom they recognised from the farm fight. The official report blamed her for draining Hobb before guards trapped and shot her. Her clean mouth and the shallow wounds and sulphurous residue on Hobb challenged that account. The party suspects poisoned arrows and a staged vampire attack; neither explanation is yet proved. Quinn took her bracelet for Isolde. All the coven members share a forearm tattoo, whose meaning remains unknown.

The two sisters
The tapestry, copied in a quiet room of the manor, names them: Celandine and Isolde. Its hem reads: “Sister for sister, thread for thread, pull the name of the one not wed.” Behind Isolde’s name was Celandine’s last letter: “He knows. Keep the boy safe if I can’t. Love, your sister.”
The farm meeting (S30)
Quinn gave Sibbet’s bracelet and Celandine’s letter to Isolde. She said Voss’s message had promised peace at a warehouse, and Sibbet had gone on the coven’s behalf. She identified Lily of the Shade as a vampire-poison source in Leon’s greenhouse. Responsibility for Sibbet’s death remains under investigation.
Isolde said Celandine had turned before marrying the old governor, and blamed him for killing her after she planned to take Leon away for treatment. She identified the old governor as the payer of the twelve years of weekly blood shipments. These are her accounts, rather than events the party witnessed.
She willingly released Odettia’s bond, with the priest’s cleansing still required. She wants to protect the true version of Leon and expects a meeting at dusk, at the farm. The coven was mourning Sibbet; a lasting settlement has not been reached. See Session 30.
A pledge of aid (S31)
At dusk, Isolde arrived with about twelve women of the coven for the meeting with Leon. She and Quinn mingled blood in an agreement to look out for one another; she pledged that she and her coven would be there if he needed them. They approached Leon, but the actual meeting and any wider settlement remain unplayed. Kaelith had meanwhile burned the greenhouse’s Lily of the Shade plants; this does not settle responsibility for Sibbet’s death. See Session 31.
The coastal refuge (S32)
Isolde met Leon and challenged his account of Celandine’s death. Two coven members separately approached Quinn, asked for protection and invited him to hunt. Later Isolde said the coven had gone days without hunting. After Odettia knocked out Leon, Isolde carried him to a refuge in the coastal caves. Several coven members were there when the party arrived. See Session 32.

npcs/corv.title: Corv
npcs/corv.content:
A human scholar-mage displaced in time. He was once tall and strong; now he is hunched, ragged and frost-rimed, and talks half to himself. He lives in the ruins north of the city and comes into town only to draw on Yara Dunwell’s preservation magic, which keeps him solid. His own magic is gone.

His story: He was researching dragon-blood magic as a time anchor, meaning only to observe the future. The scrying broke and threw him forward. That was five years ago. Memories of where he came from are fading, and his mind feels split between two times. Two years ago Yara saved his life.
The fading: Like Kaelith, he is slowly disappearing: “this time does not accept us.” When they touched hands, both their arms turned translucent to the bone. His leg once vanished entirely until he drew on Yara’s magic. He fears he will be “dust” within months.
The cure: He gave Kaelith a vial of a nearly finished cure, missing one ingredient. He calls it “the thing that does not die, the thing that consumes… it exists in shadows and consumes souls”, and traced it to the manor, where he was caught three times trying to get in. He believes the cure will take him home. The deal: he uses it, and teaches Kaelith to make her own.
He named Ilithrea Belabranta, Odettia’s ancestor, in connection with his research, then lost the memory.

In S27 the vial came alive at midnight inside the manor, its contents pooling downward.
The missing lead (S31)
Kaelith reached the room his vial had previously pointed toward, but the vial remained dormant and its former target was absent. No ingredient was recovered and no remedy completed. Kaelith remains at risk from her failing Temporal Refuge. See Session 31.
The visitor at the Green Leaf (S32)
Corv arrived in a frost-covered coat with half his face already gone. He faded completely as he reached for Kaelith. His last word was “Oblex.” Vander found a second, similar vial sewn into Corv’s robes and Kaelith took it. She took Corv’s word to be an ingredient clue. Her vial reacted towards Leon at midnight. See Session 32.

npcs/edrik-cole.title: Edrik Cole
npcs/edrik-cole.content:
Harbourmaster of Saltmere for thirty-one years. Meticulous and tight-lipped, he respects protocol over pressure or bribes. He collects the dock taxes and sends the takings up to the manor every day. He has dug 140–150 graves for bodies that washed up over the years. He also saw a griffin over the sea through his spyglass.
Quinn worked for him for a day (S25). He let slip that prisoners go through the dock to the manor’s dungeons (twelve in one day recently), and that torture equipment was signed for by the head of the Manor Guard. When he jumped into the harbour to haul out a drained body, Quinn picked his private cabinet and found:

Brennick’s arrival record, with “no departure recorded”
a mortality register with bursts of deaths, and three in the past week (taken by Quinn)
the governor’s standing exemption letting manor wagons pass uninspected, renewed for about thirty years
a large payment to the ship Tideworth, marked “agent”
his private notes on the governess’s death: “horrible death”, “body mutilated”, “inside job?” (taken by Quinn)

As far as the party knows, Cole hasn’t noticed the two missing documents yet.

npcs/gerta-wrack.title: Gerta Wrack
npcs/gerta-wrack.content:
Keeper of the Green Leaf boarding house. A stout dwarf with forearms like a smith’s, warm and fast-talking, and the owner of a magically attached third serving arm, which she uses to pour, carry and dish up stew all at once. She was born in Saltmere; her father was a manor guard.
She will gossip about anyone in town except whoever is staying under her roof: her guests’ privacy is a point of professional pride. She runs the job board the party used in S25, told Quinn the story of Brennick, and kept an eye on Laura for the party. She lent Milo a halfling tuxedo for the governor’s dinner, left behind by “a butler just about your size”.
Her stew is very good. Vander would know.
Shelter after the chase (S31)
When Vander, Milo and the disguised Osric arrived fleeing the guards, Gerta sent them into a back room and locked the door to shelter them. Kaelith followed them inside as a ladybird and changed back. They remain there at the session’s pause. See Session 31.
A visitor at the Green Leaf (S32)
Gerta announced a hooded visitor under cover of housekeeping. Corv vanished at the door. She also saw Luna squeeze through the door in mount form as Vander and Milo left after Kaelith. See Session 32.

npcs/henrietta.title: Henrietta
npcs/henrietta.content:
Seamstress of the Tailored Needle, Ropewalk Lane, Saltmere. Elderly and straight-laced, with reading glasses. She has lived fifty years in Saltmere and never left. Her shop smells of beeswax, new wool and mothballs. She called the new governor’s funeral speech “the best day of my fifty years here”.
She hired Odettia for a day (S25) and was delighted by her embroidery. She keeps a chest she can’t bring herself to open. It held Isolde’s velvet gloves. Isolde was her partner of ten years, and vanished twelve years ago without a word: “she was my everything.” Odettia promised to find out what happened.
In S27, Odettia sent word to Isolde, through Quinn, that Henrietta still waits for her. Isolde answered that she wants a life with Henrietta too.

npcs/index.title: People
npcs/index.content:
Saltmere
Leon Thrace (governor) · Isolde (coven leader) · Henrietta (seamstress) · Corv (the traveller) · Osric (Order of Aster knight) · Gerta Wrack (Green Leaf) · Edrik Cole (harbourmaster) · Laura (Harlan’s widow) · Yara Dunwell (apothecary) · Celandine, the old governor, Brennick and others
With the party
Milo Bramble · Luna, Ariane, Barry · the crew of the *Maris*
Elsewhere
People of the Sword Coast (Bearbarrow, the road, Baldur’s Gate) · People of interest (Sundar, Morgan, Aldric Mourne, the Gundwynds, Kannoth)
New in S29: Captain Voss · Halflin · Brennan.
New in S31: Julianne, the hooded guide who identified herself as Halflin’s sister, and further observations of the manor medic.

npcs/isolde.title: Isolde
npcs/isolde.content:
Leader of the vampire coven at Harlan’s farm. She was once handmaiden to the governess Celandine, and is Celandine’s sister. She was Henrietta’s partner of ten years.

Twelve years ago she vanished without a word, around the time the governess died. Henrietta has been waiting for her ever since. In Odettia’s vision (S25), seen through Isolde’s own eyes, the governess lay murdered in a torchlit dungeon.
The coven. She arrived at Harlan’s farm frightened and on the run, carrying only a tapestry of two crowned women. Laura hid her and her coven in the cellar for twelve years. They lived on animals and weekly bottled blood from the harbour.
Harlan. When Harlan beat Laura, Isolde asked her, “Do you want me to take care of this?”, then killed him. She told Laura the last human she had wanted to kill was the old governor.
S26. She watched her coven attack Osric, bit Odettia, was knocked out by Vander and spared. She claimed her coven hunts “a greater evil” in the manor that wears a familiar face, offered a guarded truce, and left as mist.
S27, in the orchard with Quinn:

“They killed my sister in front of me.” She holds everyone in the manor complicit.
She wants a life with Henrietta, but the town hunts her every night.
She offered to release Odettia’s bite in exchange for Celandine’s last letter.
She asked Quinn to let her into the manor, and doubts Leon is truly her nephew.
She will consult her coven before answering.



Appearance: an older, calm vampire with cold authority. In S27 she wore a grey, tattered dress.
The meeting at the farm (S30)
Quinn gave her Sibbet’s bracelet and Celandine’s last letter. She said Voss’s message had promised peace at a warehouse, to which she sent Sibbet. She mourned the loss and called Quinn’s gift a kindness she would not forget.
She told Quinn and Odettia that Celandine turned before her and later offered her vampirism. Celandine married the old governor after turning; he secretly provided prisoners for her feeding. Isolde said he killed Celandine after discovering her plan to take their sick son elsewhere for treatment. She also identified him as the payer of the coven’s twelve years of weekly blood shipments. These revelations are her account.
She described Leon as born with vampiric blood his body could not tolerate, subjected to failed treatments until his abrupt recovery around his father’s death. She smells sulphur on him and doubts he is her nephew. The party explained oblexes, which she did not know by name. She named Lily of the Shade in the greenhouse as a source of poison that harms vampires.
Reading her sister’s last words brought her to tears. She willingly released Odettia’s bond, directing her to a priest for cleansing. She wants to protect the true version of her nephew and expects the promised meeting with Leon at dusk, at the farm. Neither the meeting nor an unconditional promise to fight Leon has happened. See Session 30.
The dusk arrival (S31)
Isolde arrived at the farm with about twelve members of her coven, saying she had prepared for an uncertain meeting. She acknowledged Quinn had kept the agreement by bringing Leon. Calling him a true ally, she offered a pact to look out for each other. They mingled blood in a handshake, and Quinn felt a bond form. She promised her own and her coven’s aid when he needed them. They walked toward Leon; play paused before the conversation. No peace settlement or family reconciliation has happened. See Session 31.
Leon and the seaside caves (S32)
Isolde introduced herself to Leon as his aunt and told him that his father had murdered Celandine. Once she heard about his agreement with the oblex, she asked how they could remove it. She carried him to the coven’s coastal refuge after Odettia knocked him unconscious, giving the group an hour to plan. She reconsidered keeping him with her when he warned of the midnight takeover. See Session 32.

npcs/laura.title: Laura
npcs/laura.content:
Harlan’s widow, a farmer’s wife in her fifties, married to him since eighteen.

S25: Vander found her locked upstairs at the farm. She tested him by cutting herself to see whether he hungered. She said a red-eyed, clawed woman had seized Harlan and spared her. Vander buried Harlan and brought her to the Green Leaf, where Kaelith found and healed bruises on her ribs, shoulders and neck. Harlan had been beating her.
S27, her confession (for 20 more gold in her bag):

She sheltered the vampire coven in her cellar for twelve years, made sure their weekly blood arrived from the harbour in carts bearing the governor’s symbol, and fed them animals in secret. Harlan never knew.
When Harlan beat her, the coven’s leader Isolde offered to “take care of this”, and Laura said yes.
The blood supply stopped a week or two ago, and the coven has gone feral since.



She is leaving the island to start again. Luna blessed her journey.

npcs/leon-thrace.title: Leon Thrace
npcs/leon-thrace.content:
Governor of Saltmere. Human, mid-twenties. Son of the late old governor and of Celandine, who died more than ten years ago.
What the party has seen

At the funeral (S24): He threw the nobles out of his father’s funeral, seated the commoners, made a speech about a new era and declared a town-wide celebration. Odettia lingered on his arm. Odettia also saw his eyes flash crimson.
His sickroom: Quinn and Milo found his old room in the manor’s medical wing: bloodstains, potions, and shackles on all four corners of the bed, with a hidden stair down to a dungeon of prisoners.
The key: Osric saw the Order of Aster key around Leon’s neck at the funeral. At dinner a chain around his neck disappeared under his shirt.
The invitation (S25): He wrote to the party: dinner, “come armed if it comforts you”, and a claim that he knows why his people are dying.
The dinner (S27):

He talked of a lifelong illness that left him bedridden until a house medic brought a cure from overseas.
He tends his late mother’s moonflowers himself, and her portrait is missing from the gallery.
He sealed the stair to the old dungeon after his father died.
He barely eats (“a liquid diet”), drinks only from his own cellar, and retires early because of his “poor constitution”.
He offered the party 800 gp to remove the coven he blames for eight deaths.
Asked by Quinn why he would kill his own kind: “I’m sure I don’t know what you mean.”


His politics: He describes his father’s rule as brutal and fear-driven, and says his father was a softer man before Leon’s mother died. “I want to give people something to work towards rather than something to run from.”

The overheard orders (S28)
Odettia’s Clairvoyance caught a conversation at the manor desk between a doctor and another speaker she believed was Leon. The doctor discussed a dhampir’s blood that had not clotted; the sample was to be kept. The conversation described Voss shutting a girl inside a shed and his men killing her, followed by orders to burn her body and the arrows before dawn, without a crowd, and to stand the lanes down at three. The speakers’ identities were not independently confirmed.
The party’s examination of Sibbet and Hobb then challenged the official account blaming the vampire for the man’s death. See Session 28.
Early suspicions
The party wondered if he was a vampire. His mother’s sister, Isolde, called him “that thing in there” and doubts he is her nephew at all. Odettia sensed something dormant in him. See open-threads.
Isolde’s account (S30)
Isolde told Quinn and Odettia that Celandine married the old governor after becoming a vampire, and Leon inherited vampiric blood his body could not tolerate. Blood replacement, surgery and injections failed through a lifetime of illness. Celandine wanted to take him elsewhere for treatment; Isolde holds the old governor responsible for killing her after he discovered the plan.
She dates Leon’s sudden recovery to around his father’s death and says she now smells sulphur on him. The party explained oblexes to her, but what has happened to Leon remains unresolved. She requested a meeting with him at dusk. See Session 30; the raid and his response followed in Session 31.
Taken to the farm (S31)
Ariane saw the medic resting a hand on Leon’s back, with magic flowing into him. Odettia and Kaelith’s griffon raid shattered the greenhouse; the griffon seized Leon and the medic while Kaelith burned the Lily of the Shade plants. Odettia brought both men to the farm.
Leon initially disputed that Isolde was his aunt or that Celandine was murdered. Shown the cellar tapestry, he recognised his mother and her handmaiden. He admitted knowing his mother was a vampire and that he was half-vampire, and said a cure had been found. He showed recognition when Odettia named the oblex, but did not explain his cure. He also recalled seeing someone resembling Vander in town a couple of weeks earlier; Odettia’s suggestion that this was his brother remains unconfirmed.
Kaelith found an undated medical chart reporting normal daytime readings, then “agitated,” “violent,” “new powers?” at 12:30 a.m.; a receipt for a live specimen and accompanying specialist; and pipes connecting a restraint room to his bedroom. Their full meaning remains unresolved.
Leon agreed to talk to Isolde in the hope of peace, despite doubting their kinship. She has arrived with her coven; play stopped before their conversation. See Session 31.
The agreement (S32)
Leon heard Isolde’s account of Celandine’s murder. He told her and Odettia that something from Baldur’s Gate had been injected into him and that he had an agreement with the creature. He defended the use of condemned prisoners, which Odettia challenged, and proposed letting Saltmere decide after hearing his story.
In the coven’s caves he woke in distress and warned that the oblex takes control at midnight. The medic said the Order of Aster key was still on Leon’s neck, and Leon warned that removing it would make things worse. Odettia set him down in remote woodland. At midnight an altered voice answered Quinn, and Kaelith’s vial pulled towards Leon’s location. See Session 32.

npcs/milo-bramble.title: Milo Bramble
npcs/milo-bramble.content:
Halfling, sixteen. Eager and brave, and weighs about ninety pounds.

Baldur’s Gate (S12): He was a theatre helper at the Vellum Stage, hired by Aldric Mourne, and was unwittingly used as bait. The party rescued him, and he has been loyal to them ever since. He lived in a shack in the Outer City with a mattress and a lamp.
His mother: Marloes was freed from her Guild debt at sail-off (S15), through Odettia’s Guild favour, signed as “Morgan Duskbane”.
The voyage: The rigger Wren Talvas taught him to climb. He made his first kill in the sahuagin raid (S17).
Saltmere:

He infiltrated the manor with Quinn in borrowed priest’s robes (S24).
He works the taps for Gerta.
He nursed a hangover after a night on the spirits (S26).
At the governor’s table (S27) he came as Odettia’s ward in a borrowed tuxedo, with bare feet. He ate everything, then pocketed what he couldn’t eat, and politely declined Quinn’s invitation to the bathroom.



The presence he calls his father (S28)
After dinner Milo became unresponsive, silently moving his lips. Kaelith sensed overwhelming magic. When Odettia tried Identify she felt fear, grief and longing for family, then heard “This one’s mine.” Her answer, “He is his own,” was followed by a burned hand and a force that threw her back.
Milo woke confused and apologised for his “dad”. He remembered an image of two bodies on stone slabs, but could not hold onto the words. He also offered Odettia a stolen manor drink he called a healing potion; it smelled of wine and healed her. The experience left him hungry and drained. He stayed at the Green Leaf helping Gerta while the party went out. The presence’s identity remains unknown.
The farmhouse door (S29)
Odettia’s owl found him dancing at the Green Leaf and summoned him to the party. He caught up on the farm road, offered fifty gold from his tavern winnings and accompanied them to Harlan’s deserted farmhouse.
He performed a fiery working, his eyes ringed with red, and said he had set a hellish rebuke on the front door. He warned everyone to stay five feet away and marked the exclusion area in chalk. Odettia left a warning note and a request to speak to the coven later. The ward’s effect had not been tested by the end of S29. See Session 29.
The test (S30)
Wondering whether his father had exaggerated the ward, Milo threw a pebble at the front door. An enormous explosion destroyed the door and frame and left the porch sagging. Milo was covered in soot; Kaelith poured water over the fire with Elementalism, and Odettia cleaned him. The entrance is now wrecked. His father’s identity remains unknown. See Session 30.
The rope works (S31)
Milo accompanied Vander and Osric into town, acquired their disguises and carefully recorded Vander’s alias, “Uncle K.” During Vander’s pursuit of Halflin, he laid a trap at the rope works’ rear door. He said his “dad” encouraged adding more power. The blast destroyed the rear of the building and apparently killed Halflin, according to Milo; no body was examined before the escape. Milo survived and fled with his companions to the Green Leaf. His father later offered no help with Kaelith’s missing ingredient. The presence remains unidentified. See Session 31.
Session 32
Milo said he meant to keep Halflin from escaping and asked Vander if he had done the right thing. Vander cautioned him about the strength of his magic. Milo rode Luna to the farm and was carried in a griffon claw during the flight to the caves, picking up superficial cuts. See Session 32.

npcs/osric.title: Osric
npcs/osric.content:
Knight of the Order of Aster, and one of the seven companions who rode out with Vander’s father Umber and were never found at his death. Haggard, as if he has lived in the woods for days.

He tracked the Order’s stolen key to Saltmere and saw it around Leon Thrace’s neck at the old governor’s funeral. He later said a fellow knight had also reached the island but was taken by guards.
In S26 the party found him being savaged by the coven in the woods by Harlan’s farm. Vander saved and healed him, and Kaelith charmed him into telling the truth.
He saw Umber in Vander’s face. He fears Sundar, who he says has turned to Shar and is hunting the remaining members of Umber’s company, blaming them for their father’s death.
He took a room at the Green Leaf. In S27 he came in dazed, muttered “those bastards”, and stormed out again. In S28 they found him alive, bound and gagged in a cart escorted by two guards through the hidden passage. He was conscious but not fully lucid; his account of capture followed in S30.

The party’s trust in him is fragile.
The rescue (S29)
The party rescued him from the dungeon. A blind-fired bolt wounded his shoulder; Odettia healed him for five hit points, and Vander carried him out on Luna. He fell when Luna vanished and was still unconscious at Harlan’s farmhouse at the end of S29. Odettia noticed sickly-sweet breath and suspected drugging or poisoning. See Session 29.
Awake again (S30)
Vander removed his poison with Lay on Hands, and he woke asking for water. He said guards wearing a hippogriff-like crest had seized a fellow knight from their camp; his demand for justice led to his own capture. He said that companion was now dead and offered to fight alongside the party if armed.
To Vander and Kaelith, he described Umber’s killers wearing blue cloaks with gold WSS letters. A member of the company returned the key to the Order before its later theft from the reliquary. He recalled records saying the key suppressed an oblex’s ability to produce copies, and said Sundar entered a temple of Shar and, years later, killed one of the remaining companions with an arrow. These are Osric’s accounts, not events the party witnessed themselves. See Session 30.
A noble disguise (S31)
Milo acquired a pinstripe suit, top hat and monocle for Osric. He posed as a noble leading bounty hunters, talked their way through the town checkpoint and slipped gold to the guard when asked for paperwork. He accompanied Vander to the rope works and escaped with him and Milo after the explosion. He is now sheltered at the Green Leaf, alongside Kaelith and the returned Luna. See Session 31.
A watch at the Green Leaf (S32)
Osric offered to help as Vander and Milo rode after Kaelith. At Vander’s request he stayed at the Green Leaf to watch the guards. See Session 32.

npcs/people-of-interest.title: People of Interest
npcs/people-of-interest.content:
People the party is chasing, being chased by, or worried about.
Sundar Duskbane
Vander’s older brother, once a steadfast paladin of Lathander, who left on an oath of vengeance after their father’s death. At the Closed Door (S13) Vander learned Sundar sold the stolen Order of Aster key; he “seemed certain” when he did. Zivra’s prophecy says he kneels to another god. In S26 Osric said Sundar has turned to Shar and is hunting what remains of Umber’s company. In S27 a manor guard mentioned rumours of a red-haired wanderer in the Moonshaes.
In S30, Osric said Sundar entered a temple of Shar while pursuing the WSS. Years later, they met him again with a dark aura, and he shot one of their remaining companions through the skull. The survivors fled. Vander wondered whether this was still his brother; possession or replacement is unproved. See Session 30.
Morgan Duskbane
Vander’s twin sister, a fierce fighter still with the Order of Aster. She led the call to cast Vander out.
”M.D.”
Wrote to Castellar about the key and was heading to Baldur’s Gate.
Umber Duskbane
Vander’s father, a mighty paladin of Lathander. He was found dead outside Waterdeep, still gripping the key; the seven knights who rode with him vanished. Osric is one of them.
In S30, Osric described masked attackers in blue cloaks with gold WSS letters killing Umber. A member of the company returned the key to the Order before its later theft. This is Osric’s testimony. See Session 30.
Aldric Mourne
The WSS’s operative in Baldur’s Gate: posh and human, by Milo’s account. He worked out of an Outer City building with a magical ward, and hired Milo at the Vellum Stage. The buyer’s agent for the key at the Closed Door also called himself “Mourne”. Cassia’s letter narrowed the man behind the alias to four candidates, including the brothers Erstin and Renard Holloway. The party overheard the name “Holloway” in Baldur’s Gate tied to Amn–Waterdeep politics, and Neve recalled Renard Holloway being linked to negotiations.
In S32 the manor medic identified Aldric Mourne as Renard Holloway, a senior member of the WSS. He said Holloway left aboard the delivery ship and did not know his current location. See Session 32.
The Gundwynds and Deryc
The Waterdeep hippogriff-breeding family that Odettia was promised into, connected to the Black Boars. At the governor’s dinner (S27) a guard mentioned a Gundwynd trader due in Saltmere in a few days.
The Black Boars
A Baldur’s Gate gang hunting Odettia. Odettia and Kaelith fought two of them (S13) and watched them lean on Theron (S14).
Kannoth
The vampire lord whose undead hold fallen Cendriane. Kaelith barely escaped him.

npcs/saltmere-townsfolk.title: Saltmere Townsfolk
npcs/saltmere-townsfolk.content:
Major figures have their own pages: Leon Thrace · Isolde · Henrietta · Corv · Osric · Gerta Wrack · Edrik Cole · Laura · Yara Dunwell
Celandine
Leon’s mother and the old governor’s wife, called the governess. She died twelve years ago; the town was never told how. In Odettia’s vision she lay murdered in a torchlit dungeon with a wound across her chest. Her portrait is missing from the manor gallery. Moonflowers and sea bass were her favourites. She was Isolde’s sister: a tapestry hidden in the manor names them both. Her last letter to Isolde reads: “He knows. Keep the boy safe if I can’t.”
The old governor
Leon’s father, buried in S24. He ruled by fear, with punishments, whippings and hangings. Henrietta says his cruelty began about when the governess died. Leon says he was softer before. He died of illness after working himself into the ground. He signed the standing order letting manor wagons pass the docks uninspected.
Harlan
A Saltmere farmer, and not the same person as Harlan of the Loose Rigger in Baldur’s Gate. His livestock were drained of blood. He was killed by the coven after beating his wife Laura, rose as a feral undead and was destroyed by Vander (S25). He is buried under the oak by his fence.
Brennick
A foreign hunter who came to Saltmere decades ago, asked about the old ruling family, went up the manor road and never came back. Gerta remembers the mark stitched on his gear: two crossed lines through a closed eye, the same mark as in Quinn’s book. Cole’s arrival record lists him as “hunter” of the Talen family, and notes “no departure recorded”.
The Father
Saltmere’s elderly, slow-moving chapel priest, known simply as “Father”. Odettia effectively ran the old governor’s funeral for him. Vampire bites are his old speciality, and he knows how to cure Odettia’s (S27). During the chapel investigation in S28, a guard said he was gone; the party has not established where he is.
Voss
One of Leon’s guards. He warned the party about drawing weapons at dinner and has heard of “a red-haired wanderer” elsewhere in the Moonshaes. In the conversation Odettia overheard in S28, Voss was named as the man who shut the girl inside the shed before his men killed her. This was an overheard account, not an event the party witnessed. The party has now met several people named Voss: the tavern owner Sable Voss, and Ser Callum Voss, Marianne’s former owner.
Sable Voss
Keeps a tavern in town.
Fenna
A mother whose feverish son Kaelith cured with marshmallow leaf (S25). She named her “Kaelith the Wise”.
Cole’s office and the docks
See Edrik Cole.
Sibbet
A member of Isolde’s coven, recognised from the farm fight. In S28 the party identified her dead body in the chapel’s medical room. A report accused her of draining Hobb before guards trapped and shot her in a salt workshop. Her mouth was clean, and the bodies’ condition challenged that account. She had real vampiric canines and the coven’s shared forearm tattoo. Quinn took her metal, vine-like bracelet to show Isolde. An overheard order called for her body and the arrows to be burned on the cliff before dawn.
Hobb
A human whose body lay beside Sibbet’s in the chapel’s medical room (S28). The official report named him as her victim, with an instruction to display his body as a warning. Examination found life-force draining unlike ordinary vampire feeding, shallow neck wounds and sulphurous residue on exposed skin. A knife lay on the slab. The party suspects the bite marks were staged; the killer has not been established.
Captain Voss
Captain of Leon’s guard, recognised by his voice beyond the reinforced dungeon door in S29. He told the party to take Osric and the prisoners and leave, invoked the governor’s authority and then sounded an alarm warning of an approaching battalion. He is the brother of Ser Callum Voss, the paladin encountered during Reza Sahil’s contests; the captain’s first name is not established here. See Session 29.
Halflin
Elf, one of the twins freed from the dungeon in S29. Vander found his charge sheet on a guard and retains it. The paper lists numerous alleged offences and a scheduled extraction. Halflin escaped; Vander later pursued him through the rope works in S31. Milo’s trap apparently killed him, but no body was examined before the party fled. His reported death coincided with Luna’s return and Vander’s restored blessing. See Session 29 and Session 31.
Brennan
A boy freed from the dungeon in S29. He said he had been falsely accused of theft and transported by boat; he appeared frightened and sincere. Odettia sent her owl to guide him, and Vander later gave him money for lodging at the Green Leaf. See Session 29.
Julianne
A hooded rapier-wielder who introduced herself by this name in S31; her face remained concealed. She helped Vander’s disguised group enter Saltmere, then sold him a lead to Halflin at the docks’ rope works. On leaving, she said Halflin’s sister sent her regards, identifying herself as that sister. No surname or later allegiance is known. See Session 31.
The manor medic
The medic who treated Quinn at dinner was beside Leon in the greenhouse in S31, a hand on his back and magic flowing into him. The griffon seized both men; the medic was taken to Harlan’s farm and pinned and under Odettia’s Suggestion against using magic on her or her allies. See Session 31. In Session 32 he claimed to have been a mage at the High College of Waterdeep and admitted WSS membership under Zone of Truth. He knew of Leon’s agreement and the key around his neck. Vander freed him and he fled. His name and current whereabouts are unknown.

npcs/sword-coast-people.title: People of the Sword Coast
npcs/sword-coast-people.content:
Daggerford and Bearbarrow
Priya Nagorth

A tiefling merchant who hauls goods along the Sword Coast. The party escorted her wagon out of Daggerford. Something in her cargo, a strongbox marked WSS, turned out to be far more dangerous than she knew.
Losandra Ayling

A tall orc, the constable of Bearbarrow and its only law. The party convinced her that the stable hand had been replaced by an ooze creature. Odettia has written to her and is still waiting for a reply.
Isaac Townsend

The jovial red-haired dwarf who keeps Bearbarrow’s inn.
Julius

Bearbarrow’s teenage stable hand, with a red scarf. He was taken and replaced by the oblex.
Bram Hallow
Losandra’s deputy. A creature dragged him into the mine beneath Edda Fenlow’s house, and he woke the next morning insisting that someone must be told the name Aldric.
Edda Fenlow
A Bearbarrow gardener who vanished from her farm the morning after the wagon arrived. Her cellar hid a path into the old mine.
Ferris and Cade Holt

Halfling brothers and petty criminals, held in Losandra’s cell. They were paid to cause a disturbance at the inn so that Julius could reach the wagon, and they swear they knew nothing more.
Tomas Geld, Denny and the Voss family
Tomas Geld is Bearbarrow’s dwarf carpenter, who lost a whole day of memory to the oblex. Denny is the baker, who wants proper walls. Marta Voss was replaced by a copy, which the party destroyed. Her mother-in-law, Old Petra Voss, had known for two days that it was not Marta.
Sister Wren

A travelling healer who arrived in Bearbarrow a few days before the wagon, selling remedies from a cart in the square. She heard people running to the well in the night.
The road south
The gnome on the road

A gnome with a cart, met on the road south of Bearbarrow. His name is not recorded.
Morvin and Rilla Kettlebottom
Halfling siblings who sell candles and soap along the Sword Coast, and argue about which inn has the best beds. Vander bought candles from them.
Zivra

The fortune-teller at the carnival who gave three of the party their prophecies (S8).
Gordo Plank

A relics dealer on the road into the Fields of the Dead, whose mule Duchess will not cross after dark. His relics are fake, but his warning about the Fields was not.
Harsk
A retired Flaming Fist soldier turned turnip farmer, stranded at the ford with other travellers by a wyvern (S9).
Cassia

A former Waterdeep City Watch investigator, Cassia Torn, who rode into Bearbarrow at Priya’s call and travelled south with the party. Briefed the party on the WSS (S10). Her letter at sea (S16) narrowed “Aldric Mourne” down to four men, two of them the brothers Erstin and Renard Holloway.
Aldren Thace
His letter reached the party in S10, and Vander delivered it to Brother Callum in Baldur’s Gate.
Baldur’s Gate
Theron Vale

The Belabranta family steward, a half-elf with a military bearing, and Odettia’s childhood tutor. He posted a 500 gp reward for her. She confronted him in disguise (S11), and the party later watched the Black Boars threaten him (S14).
Orin Castellar

Owner of the Closed Door, an invitation-only antiques showroom in the Upper City. Through him the party learned Sundar sold the Order of Aster key (S13). Kaelith bought a Cendriane emerald there.
Others

Bessa Ironhand: keeper of the Lizard’s Cradle, the party’s base, where Vander holds the stew record (8 bowls).
Thalwick: bookseller on the Basilisk Gate, who sold the party a book (S15).
Brother Callum: Shrine of the Moonmaiden.
Harlan of the Loose Rigger: a harbour-bar contact, and not Saltmere’s farmer.
Dane Copperweight: a jeweller whose cellar the party cleared (S14). It connects to the sewers, and he now believes someone matching Odettia fled down there.
Edren Gale: a wizard who teleported to the Black Boars’ hideout (S14).
Crane: a Black Boars figure.
Marloes: Milo’s mother.

At sea
Reza Sahil
The pirate whose three contests the party took on (S18): a drawn duel, the befriending of Biscuit, and a card game Odettia won. The prizes included a replacement chart and the greatsword Marianne, taken from Ser Callum Voss.

npcs/the-maris.title: The Maris and Her Crew
npcs/the-maris.content:
The ship that carried the party from Baldur’s Gate to the Moonshaes (S15–S23). It has since left Saltmere.
Neve Saren

Captain, about seventy, a retired sailor who inherited the Maris from her father, the last of a sailing family. She has sailed past Viledel some forty times and had never seen its lighthouse dark. She carries a debt on the ship that came to light in Saltmere (S23). She wears an emerald necklace that Kaelith recognised as Cendriane work, and it grew warm during Kaelith’s fading in the storm. She was washed overboard in that storm and rescued by the party (Kaelith in shark form, Vander hauling her in). In S25 she delivered Odettia’s parents’ letter to the Green Leaf on a night visit, then left on an errand to a southern island.
Bran Korr

The cook: a half-orc in his late fifties who has not spoken in twenty years. He talks with gestures, a slate and very expressive eyebrows. He is gentle, slips extra food to whoever looks worst, makes excellent pastries, and carves little wooden animals. At the drowned wreck (S19) he collapsed sobbing, and a cache of his carvings was found aboard. By the end of the kraken escape he seemed steadier than he had in years.
Wren Talvas

The rigger: early twenties, from Amn, four years aboard, and she lives in the crow’s nest. Chatty, optimistic, never surprised. She fled her own wedding the night before and won’t talk about it. She took Milo under her wing and taught him to climb the rigging.
Quinn
Found in the hold during the voyage. See Quinn.

npcs/yara-dunwell.title: Yara Dunwell
npcs/yara-dunwell.content:
Herbalist and apothecary of Saltmere, nearly twenty years in the trade. Short, with sleeves pushed up and forearms stained two colours. She is better at bookkeeping and customers than at growing things, by her own account.
Her drying herbs hang in twinkling bubbles of preservation magic, words taught to her by a frost-covered traveller whose life she saved: Corv. Near that magic, Kaelith feels solid in time. Corv returns to drain it to stay whole.
She hired Kaelith for a day (S25), sells her hangover cure (“Antivomix”, 50% to Kaelith), and charged a sick child’s mother only a copper. “Anytime you want to make a few bucks…”
Quinn’s visit (S31)
Quinn described the increasing pressure of the lighthouse-orb curse. Yara believed it could wrench spirit from body and told him to find someone skilled in soul magic, likely in a larger settlement. She could not remove it herself.
Using herbs and preservation words, she gave him an experimental amber bottle with three doses. A dose helps his next resistance check within twenty-four hours; it does not remove the curse.
