She asked him to report the result. He also bought Poison of Silence for fifty gold, enough for roughly five arrows and described as interfering with magic. Its detailed effects were left unexplored. See Session 31.

open-threads.title: Open Threads
open-threads.content:
Urgent

Leon and the oblex. Leon warned that the oblex takes control at midnight. He was last seen in remote woodland with the key still around his neck. The medic suspects their souls are joined, and separation remains untested. Leon’s proposed account to Saltmere and public decision have yet to happen.
Kaelith, the vials and Barry. Corv vanished after saying “Oblex.” Kaelith has both vials and one reacted towards Leon at midnight. Her forearm is still missing, and Barry’s fate is unknown after their link went silent.
Odettia’s cleansing. Isolde released the bond in S30. Odettia has roughly twenty-four hours left to find the Father and complete the rite.
The coastal figure and the medic. Vander freed the medic, who ran from the caves. Odettia spotted a figure on the coast and sent Ariane. The figure’s identity and the medic’s passage off the island are unresolved.
The search force. The troops reached the farm’s vicinity. The party escaped to the caves and Kaelith hid their trail. Osric stayed at the Green Leaf to watch the guards.
Quinn’s orb curse. Yara’s temporary aid and recommendation to seek a soul-magic specialist still stand. No dose was recorded in S32.

Saltmere

The cleaned dungeon. The cells were empty and scrubbed; the end door was ajar. Kaelith found restraint chairs, sulphurous residue and pipes reaching Leon’s bedroom. Staff discussed a prisoner transfer in two days, involving about ten or eleven people. Their intended use was not disclosed. The warehouse has a replacement guardian and further Gundwynd-marked carts.
The greenhouse ledger. Names, dates spanning five years and tallies headed “cuttings.” What do they record? Kaelith burned the greenhouse’s Lily of the Shade plants, but no wider supply was investigated.
Halflin and the escapees. Milo’s trap apparently killed Halflin in the rope works; no body was examined. Luna and Vander’s blessing were restored. Other escapees and the fate of Halflin’s alleged victims remain unresolved. The hooded woman calling herself Julianne identified herself as his sister.
Vander’s shoulder. No treatment of his strained right shoulder was shown in S31. Divine restoration does not establish that this injury healed.
Sibbet and Hobb. Isolde says Voss’s peace message sent Sibbet to a warehouse. The bodies challenged the official account. Who arranged the deaths? The exact poison and responsibility remain unproved. The cliff smoke seen in S30 does not confirm the ordered burning of Sibbet’s body and arrows.
Celandine’s death. Isolde blamed the old governor after Celandine planned to take Leon elsewhere for treatment. Odettia’s vision showed the fatal wound, rather than the killer. Isolde told Leon her account in S32. His response left the dispute open.
Henrietta and Isolde. Odettia promised Henrietta the truth; their reunion and future remain unresolved.
The blood shipments. Isolde identified the old governor as the payer of twelve years’ weekly supply. Why did it stop? Her new promise of aid to Quinn does not settle the coven’s future feeding.
Brennick. The Talen hunter who went up the manor road and never came back. No new discovery about him occurred in S31.
The Tideworth’s cargo. Leon’s promised information and the new receipt may offer leads; their full connection remains unknown.
Osric’s testimony and the key. His accounts link Umber’s killers to WSS cloaks and suggest the key suppresses oblex copies. That property has not been tested, and the key has not been recovered.
Milo’s “dad.” The presence remains unidentified. Its encouragement preceded the rope-works explosion; it offered no help with Kaelith’s ingredient. Gerta sheltered them after the rope-works flight in S31. Milo left with Vander in S32.
Leon’s bounty offer. No completion or payment of the offer to remove the coven was recorded. The party instead brought him to Isolde.
Cole’s missing documents. His response to the stolen records has not been played.

Wider world

Sundar and the surviving knights. Leon recalls seeing someone resembling Vander in Saltmere a couple of weeks earlier; Odettia suggested his brother, but this identification is unconfirmed.
The Gundwynds. A trader is due; carts bearing their crest continue to appear on the prisoner route.
The WSS and Renard Holloway. The medic identified Renard as Aldric Mourne. His current whereabouts, the main lab’s address in Waterdeep and the locations of the two other samples remain open.
The spiderweb coins and the kraken spawn, still out at sea.
Losandra’s reply to Odettia’s letter.

places/cendriane.title: Cendriane
places/cendriane.content:
The eladrin city of Kaelith’s birth, in the Feywild: a city of the elves’ great age, and Kaelith’s home some twelve thousand years ago. It fell in the war between the eladrin and the drow, just after her parents’ spell sent her forward in time. Today it is overrun by undead under the vampire lord Kannoth. Kaelith tried to return once and barely escaped.

A crossing point lies in eladrin ruins on the Sword Coast, found by Kaelith in S10. The ruins’ writing calls it a gate. She also heard tales of another crossing at the site of her ancient village, which the vampire lord now holds.
Cendriane emeralds are worn by her people’s descendants, as her mother’s jewellery and Captain Neve Saren’s necklace show. The emerald Kaelith bought in Baldur’s Gate crumbled to dust in the storm (S16), and her fading stopped.

places/index.title: Places
places/index.content:
Saltmere: the Moonshae harbour town where the party is now, with the manor, the Green Leaf, the Tailored Needle, the apothecary, the harbour and Harlan’s farm
The Sword Coast: Daggerford, Bearbarrow, the road south, Baldur’s Gate and Waterdeep
The voyage west: the storm, the wreck, the kraken spawn and the Viledel lighthouse
Cendriane: Kaelith’s lost city

places/saltmere.title: Saltmere
places/saltmere.content:
A small harbour town in the Korinn Archipelago of the Moonshae Isles, governed from a walled manor on the hill. It smells of tar, wet rope, fish guts and woodsmoke, with gulls loud over the quay. The docks are the only way in or out. The party arrived in S23, just as the old governor was buried, and found the town still celebrating days later under its new governor, Leon Thrace.

The manor

A walled hilltop estate with a formal garden, an apple orchard behind it and one main gatehouse.
What the party has seen inside:

Medical wing (S24): a working infirmary for townsfolk. Off it is the young lord’s old room: bloodstains on the stones, potions everywhere, and shackles on all four bed corners. A loose brick hides a spiral stair down.
Portrait gallery (S27): generations of governors, and a pale gap where Leon’s mother’s portrait hung.
East wing (S27): a door to the old dungeon stair, nailed shut by Leon.
Rooftop conservatory (S27): Leon’s moonflowers and his paper-strewn desk.
Dining hall (S27): a round table, a hundred-candle chandelier on a chain from the upper gallery, stained-glass windows, a great hearth. Doors lead to the garden balcony, the kitchens and the hallway.
A quiet side room (S27): holds a tapestry of two crowned women, named Celandine and Isolde.


The governor’s table (S27).
The hidden passage and dungeon
From the young lord’s room, a spiral stair runs about ten minutes down to a cold, torchlit tunnel with cart tracks. It passes a row of cells: ten empty and bloodstained, scratched with tallies and initials, and one holding fifteen shackled prisoners (S24). The tunnel runs on to the storehouse by the quay and has been heavily guarded since the break-in. In S27 Kaelith’s vial pointed down, toward whatever lies beneath the manor.
The storehouse

Near the quay, where the tunnel comes up. Its guardian, a dormant orb that unfolded into a four-metre speaking sentinel, was destroyed by Vander and Kaelith (S24). A desk ledger logged carts in and out over the last two weeks (taken by Vander).
The Green Leaf
The party’s base: a boarding house with a hand-painted sign, warm windows, cheap rooms, good stew and a job board, run by Gerta Wrack and her three arms. Milo works the taps. Osric took a room here.
The Tailored Needle
Henrietta’s shop on Ropewalk Lane: bolts of cloth, garments in the window, and a smell of beeswax, new wool and mothballs.
Yara Dunwell’s apothecary

Herbs dry in bubbles of preservation magic along the shop front. It smells of chamomile, tallow and vinegar. See Yara Dunwell.
The harbour and the harbourmaster’s office
Edrik Cole’s domain: ledgers, a locked oak cabinet, and the manifests of every crate. “Wine” bound for Harlan’s farm turned out to be blood.
The chapel

A chapel and graveyard, where the old governor’s funeral was held (S24) and where the priest who can cure Odettia’s bite sits over his stew.
Harlan’s farm
About a mile out along the main road: a stone house and slate-roofed barn above a sea cliff. Harlan lies buried under the oak by the fence. A hidden hatch in the farmhouse leads to the coven’s lair: hundreds of empty blood bottles, a tapestry of two crowned women, and years of animal bones behind it. A belt of woods lies to the north, where the Order of Aster’s symbol is carved into a tree and where the party fought the coven (S26).
The ruins to the north
Where Corv shelters.
Elsewhere in town
The market square, a forge and a jeweller (visited S23), and Sable Voss’s tavern.
The return underground (S28)
The party entered through the guarded cave route and followed two guards transporting Osric, bound and gagged in a cart. At about three in the morning they reached a cell corridor holding about fifteen prisoners. Black, smoky tendrils connected the captives to something beyond a closed door at the corridor’s end, passing through cracks beneath it.
At the end of S28 the party was fighting the two escorts and two guards by the door. One tendril had been severed by fire; the source had not been identified.
Earlier that night the party investigated the chapel’s side medical room, finding the bodies of Sibbet and Hobb on stone slabs and an incident report contradicted by their examination. They entered by the rear door, then relocked it. The Father was absent. See Session 28.
The escape before dawn (S29)
Eight prisoners escaped and four died. The party killed the two nearby guards and rescued Osric. Odettia recognised the Gundwynd crest on the bloodstained, scratched shipping container used as his cart. The reinforced door remained unopened: ice resisted Kaelith’s fire, her ritual detected an ice mage beyond it, and Captain Voss sounded an alarm. Quinn reported four people and unidentified mist through a ventilation opening.
The party escaped through the warehouse route as alarms spread and the town locked down. They settled at Harlan’s deserted farmhouse around dawn. Milo said he had warded its front door and marked a five-foot exclusion area; Odettia left a warning. Quinn smelled blood toward the cellar but deferred investigating. See Session 29.
After the rest (S30)
The party rested at Harlan’s farm. Vander removed Osric’s poison, waking him; Kaelith’s left forearm vanished and did not return. Quinn and Odettia met Isolde beneath a shaded tree nearby, gave her the letter and bracelet, and promised a meeting with Leon at dusk. Isolde named Lily of the Shade in the manor greenhouse as a vampire-poison source.
Milo’s ward exploded when he tested it with a pebble, destroying the farmhouse door and frame and damaging the porch. Odettia then called the watchtower griffon. She and Kaelith mounted it for a planned manor raid; the approach and outcome have not been played. See Session 30.
The raid, search and pursuit (S31)
The manor greenhouse was breached by a griffon, its roof shattered and its Lily of the Shade plants burned. Odettia took Leon and the medic to Harlan’s farm. Kaelith found a “cuttings” ledger, a receipt for a live specimen and accompanying specialist, and an undated chart describing Leon as violent after midnight.
The dungeon had at least thirty guards and new checkpoints. Its former cell corridor was scrubbed clean and empty. Beyond the now-ajar end door were two restraint chairs beneath pipes, staff reviewing a transfer in two days, and sulphurous residue. The pipes reached Leon’s bedroom. Corv’s vial was dormant. At the warehouse a replacement orb-form guardian and further Gundwynd-marked carts were in place.
At the docks, the rear of the rope works was destroyed by Milo’s explosive trap during Vander’s pursuit of Halflin. The fugitive was apparently killed; the rope-maker survived. Vander, Osric and Milo fled the guards, and Gerta sheltered them in the Green Leaf’s back room. Kaelith rejoined them there.
At dusk Isolde and her coven arrived at Harlan’s farm, where Quinn formed a blood bond of mutual aid with her. They approached Leon, with the conversation still to come. A large search force was fanning out in the griffon’s flight direction; its arrival at the farm has not been played. See Session 31.
The seaside caves (S32)
Isolde brought Leon to a coven refuge in a series of openings in the cliffs. Bones and old campfires lay outside, and the party found several coven members around a fire inside. Kaelith detected vampiric and necrotic magic. The medic was questioned there and ran after Vander freed him. Odettia later saw a figure moving on the coastline and sent Ariane to investigate. See Session 32.

places/sword-coast.title: The Sword Coast
places/sword-coast.content:
Daggerford

Where the adventure began (Sessions 1–5). The town had been reinforced by Waterdeep amid rising tension with Amn. Here the party answered a call for caravan guards. The full story of these first sessions is on early-sessions.

Bearbarrow

A small village on the road, where Priya Nagorth’s wagon stopped for the night (Sessions 6–7). Something got out of her cargo, replaced the stable hand Julius, and slipped down the well. The party exposed the impostor to Constable Losandra Ayling, cleared the old mine beneath the village, and found the WSS strongbox.

































Julius, the stable handIsaac Townsend, the innkeeperLosandra Ayling, the constablePriya Nagorth and her wagonSister WrenThe halfling brothers
The road south

A gnome with a cart and two halfling candle-sellers, then the carnival Marvelo’s Magnificent Midway, where Zivra read three fortunes (S8). The Fields of the Dead are a valley of cairns, the graves of the Waterdeep and Amn armies from the battle of the Winding River. Beyond them, an old watchtower by a ford was the roost of a wyvern, until a griffon returned to it and woke Odettia’s amulet (S9). Eladrin ruins, almost entirely underground, holding a crossing point toward Cendriane (S10).
Baldur’s Gate


Outer City: the Lizard’s Cradle (the party’s base, kept by Bessa Ironhand; Vander’s stew record); Aldric Mourne’s warded building; the Basilisk Gate market, with Thalwick’s Books; Dane Copperweight’s jewellery shop, whose cellar breaks into the sewers; Milo’s shack; a Black Boars tavern.
Lower City: the Loose Rigger harbour bar, the docks, and the Vellum Stage theatre where the party found Milo.
Upper City: the Closed Door (Orin Castellar’s invitation-only antiques showroom) and the Shrine of the Moonmaiden. Getting in takes persuasion or a bribe.

Waterdeep
Home of the Belabrantas, the Gundwynds, the Order of Aster’s Spires of the Morning, a church of Selûne, and the Waterdeep Scientific Society. The Society’s main laboratory is in the city. Its precise site remains unknown.

places/the-sea.title: The Voyage West
places/the-sea.content:
The Maris sailed from Baldur’s Gate at dawn (S15), chasing the Tideworth toward the Moonshae Isles. A crossing meant to take days took weeks.

The storm (S16): Kaelith faded nearly to the elbow, Neve went overboard, and Odettia’s wings became known.
Sahuagin raid (S17): a night attack led by a priestess. The raiders left coins stamped with a spiderweb and a fish head. Milo made his first kill.
Sabotage and drift (S18): the chart was burned and the compass fouled. A stowaway, Quinn, was found in the hold. The pirate Reza Sahil and his three contests.
The wreck on the sandbank (S19): the coins grew warmer as the ship approached a grounded Waterdeep navy wreck. Its drowned crew rose against the party. Aboard they found a ship’s log of a Moonshae mission some fifteen years back, a cap of water breathing, and a cache of Bran’s carved animals. Below lay a fish-headed idol. Then the sea drained back and a kraken spawn’s tentacle rose.
Escape (S20): four desperate rounds. The kraken spawn dragged the wreck under and let them go.

Viledel Lighthouse

A lighthouse on a lonely isle that Neve had never seen dark in forty passings. It was dark. The party destroyed an allip on the approach (S20), then a dread wight and a dread wraith inside, and relit the beacon (S21). Quinn looked into the lighthouse orb mid-fight and was struck senseless, the start of his Orb Curse. A keeper’s diary mentioned the Tideworth.

The top of the lighthouse.
From Viledel it was two more days to Saltmere (S22).

sessions/early-sessions.title: Daggerford to the Fields of the Dead (Sessions 1–10)
sessions/early-sessions.content:
These sessions were not recorded. This page is rebuilt from the DM’s own notes and the pictures shown at the table, so it is lighter than the later write-ups. If something here is wrong or missing, tell the DM.
Daggerford (Sessions 1–5)

The campaign opened on the first day of Tarsakh. Waterdeep had reinforced Daggerford because of rising tension with Amn, which feared an attack. The party answered a call for caravan guards (the poster is in the gallery) and took a contract from the tiefling merchant Priya Nagorth: escort her wagon of goods along the Sword Coast. Among the cargo was a strongbox stamped with the initials WSS. Priya did not know what was inside it.
Before the wagon left, each character spent a couple of hours preparing for the journey. The road out of Daggerford held several incidents: a flooded road, a woman feigning distress while her partner tried to rob the party, and a caravan inspection as they left the city. Beyond that, nothing survives in the notes.
Bearbarrow (Sessions 6–7)

The first night. Dusk found the wagon at Bearbarrow, a small village on the road, and the party took rooms at Isaac Townsend’s inn. Later that night they heard a sharp crash and a muffled scream from behind the tavern, where the wagon was parked. In the yard lay a shattered jar and the stable hand’s red scarf, with a trail of ooze and blood leading from the wagon to the village well. The session ended as something slipped into the well.
The morning after. Julius, the stable hand, walked into the tavern at breakfast, healthy and cheerful. The party did not believe it. They persuaded Constable Losandra Ayling that “Julius” was really an ooze creature wearing his face. Her deputy Bram Hallow reported that the gardener Edda Fenlow had not turned up for work. Her house looked ordinary, but a hidden path led from the cellar into an old mine. In the tunnel something pale and slick seized Bram and dragged him into the dark. The party chased it through a collapsing passage, fought the spawn of Julius and Edda in the first chamber, and climbed back out.
Rounding up the village. Back above ground the party worked with Losandra to account for everyone:

Ferris and Cade Holt, halfling brothers, sat in the village cell. They had been paid to start a disturbance at the inn that night so that Julius could reach the wagon unwatched. They did not know what was in the strongbox or what had happened to Julius afterwards.
Priya had gone through her papers and laid three documents on the inn table: her contract (marked with a stylised eye inside a circle, the WSS mark), a manifest for “one sealed research container, handle with care”, and a letter hidden in the strongbox’s false bottom, addressed to “the Society” and signed Aldric. It spoke of a “secondary site” being prepared. Priya, who had carried goods up and down the coast for years, asked: “Was I carrying something alive?”
Tomas Geld, the dwarf carpenter, was found at his farm with ooze on him. It slid off as the party came near. He had lost a whole day of memory, “like a floor where a staircase used to be”.
Denny, the baker, came when summoned and complained about the lack of walls. Sister Wren, a travelling healer with a cart in the square, had heard people running toward the well in the night.
Marta Voss had been replaced as well. The party and Losandra confronted the copy at the house on the west lane and destroyed it. Marta’s mother-in-law Old Petra Voss, bedridden, had known for two days that it was not her Marta. Losandra, who had known Marta for thirty years, told her gently that Marta was gone.

The night in the inn. Vander gave a speech to the gathered villagers, they raised their glasses, and everyone slept.
The second morning. Fresh horse tracks in the mud showed that a rider had sat at the south tree line for two hours in the night, watching the inn, then left before dawn. Bram woke and said only one thing: “Aldric. Tell someone: Aldric.” Minutes later Cassia Torn, Priya’s contact, rode in. She read the tracks as a scout, not a team, with the team half a day behind. She also gave the party a name and an address: Aldric Mourne, in Baldur’s Gate’s Outer City.
The mine. The party went back down through Edda’s cellar. The old Corwick silver mine ran down through an assay room full of forty-year-old records, a passage of alcoves where the oblex kept the stolen voices of the people it had taken, and a flooded shaft, to the oblex in its deepest chamber. Some of the voices in the alcoves were scraps of the party’s own memories. Cassia did not go down with them. The party destroyed the oblex with fire. Priya, shaken, decided to carry on to Baldur’s Gate to find Aldric Mourne, and Cassia travelled with them.
See oblexes-and-the-wss for what an oblex is and what the party knows of the WSS.
The road south (Session 8)

The wagon headed south with Priya driving and Cassia silent in the back.

A gnome with a cart stopped the party on the road. (He is the “gnome on the road” in the gallery; the DM does not remember his name.)
Morvin and Rilla Kettlebottom, halfling siblings who sell hand-dipped candles and soap between towns, sat on a boulder at a crossroads sharing bread and cheese while arguing about which inn on the road has the best beds. They tried to recruit the party to either side, and to sell them candles; Vander bought some.
Marvelo’s Magnificent Midway: a small carnival in a meadow off the road, with violet and gold wagons and lantern lines. Its ringmaster, Madame Zivra, a tiefling in a violet coat and a crooked top hat, could not stop making puns. Games cost 2 copper and paid brass prize tokens; the party played every game on the midway, including arm wrestling against a half-orc tent rigger (the “arm-wrestling orc” in the gallery).
In her tent Zivra gave Kaelith, Odettia and Vander the three prophecies. The wagon rolled on into the evening in near silence.

The Fields of the Dead (Session 9)

Gordo Plank, a weathered man with a mule named Duchess, sold “genuine artifacts of the Fields of the Dead”: rusty swords, a dented helmet and a bent arrowhead that he said had killed a famous general, each with its own grand story. When the party took him seriously he dropped the act and warned them: cross in daylight, stay on the road, never camp between the cairns, and if you hear voices, “it’s the wind”.
The Fields themselves are a vast, flat valley of cairns, the graves of the armies of Waterdeep and Amn that fought at the Winding River about two hundred years ago. One cairn is taller than the rest, with names carved in both languages. Cassia had crossed four times and never stayed for the night; Priya, six times, without looking.
On the road lay a dead ox with talon marks, a wrecked wagon, and a camp of stranded travellers at the ford led by Harsk, a retired Flaming Fist soldier. He said a young wyvern was nesting in the ruined watchtower beyond the crossing, and that the Fist patrols had been pulled into Baldur’s Gate, leaving the road unwatched. The party planned their approach, with Cassia’s crossbow in support, and killed the wyvern.

Odettia knew the iron perch rings on the tower wall: they were griffon fittings, the design her family uses at the Belabranta estate. After the fight a real griffon returned to its roost. It looked at Odettia, lowered its head, and let her stand near it. Her family amulet, the Griffontack, grew warm. The party crossed the ford and camped at the southern edge of the Fields, where Cassia mentioned a contact on the Baldur’s Gate docks named Harlan.
The ruins and Cassia’s briefing (Session 10)
The party reached eladrin ruins, almost entirely underground. Kaelith felt the traces of magic there were strong, and found writing describing the place as a gate. She also learned of tales of another crossing point, at the site of her ancient village, which is now held by the vampire lord (see cendriane). A woman named Thistle was there too. A drake ambush followed (the drakes and the cold camp are in the gallery), and during it a thief made off with the strongbox. The party never learned who it was and guessed the WSS. At the cold camp Cassia told them what she knew. The WSS was experimenting with oblexes in order to replace people of power. She had been investigating Aldric Mourne and had seven possible names for him, two of them the Holloway brothers. She also told them about the other oblex she had gone to investigate, and the sea cave north of Waterdeep where it was sealed. A pilgrim, Aldren Thace, gave Vander a letter for Brother Callum. From there the road led to Baldur’s Gate.

sessions/index.title: Session Log
sessions/index.content:
Session numbers follow the DM’s campaign record. On 1 October 2026 every session was renumbered +5 to count the five Daggerford sessions at the start. Older notes may use the old numbers.
The first ten sessions, with no recordings, are gathered on early-sessions. Sessions with a full page: 25 · 26 · 27 · 28 · 29 · 30 · 31 · 32.
Daggerford













#Session1–5Daggerford. The party gathers in Daggerford and takes a contract escorting Priya Nagorth’s wagon. No recordings or notes beyond the map and the caravan-guards poster in the gallery. See early-sessions.
Bearbarrow and the road south

























#Session6–7Bearbarrow. Something escapes Priya’s wagon and replaces the stable hand Julius: an oblex. The party exposes it, clears the mine below the village, and finds a strongbox marked WSS.8Road South. A carnival; the fortune-teller Zivra delivers three prophecies.9Fields of the Dead. A wyvern fight; a griffon at an old watchtower; the Griffontack awakens.10Eladrin Ruins. Kaelith finds a crossing point toward Cendriane. In a drake ambush a thief steals the strongbox. Cassia briefs the party on the WSS; a letter from Aldren Thace.
Baldur’s Gate





























#Session11Arrival in Baldur’s Gate. Theron Vale’s reward poster for Odettia. Shopping at the Basilisk Gate; Thace’s letter delivered to the Shrine of the Moonmaiden. Odettia confronts Theron in disguise.12Investigation. Leads from Harlan at the Loose Rigger about the Tideworth; a fight at the Vellum Stage; the party meets Milo and Neve Saren and overhears the name “Holloway”.13Three Heartbeats. At the Closed Door: Sundar sold the key, the buyer’s agent was “Mourne”, and a letter signed “M.D.” Odettia fights the Black Boars. Vander sets the stew record at the Lizard’s Cradle (8 bowls). Dreams.14The Last Day. Spying on Theron as the Black Boars lean on him; the wizard Edren Gale teleports to the Boars’ hideout. The party clears a jeweller’s cellar connected to the sewers and plants a false trail.15Sail-Off. Thalwick’s book bought. Milo’s mother Marloes freed from her Guild debt (Odettia signs as “Morgan Duskbane”). A coastal chart; a vision at Luna’s shrine. The Maris sails at dawn.
The voyage





































#Session16Storm at Sea. Cassia’s letter narrows “Aldric Mourne” to four men, including the brothers Erstin and Renard Holloway. Kaelith’s fading surges and her emerald crumbles, stopping it. Neve goes overboard and is rescued. Odettia’s wings become common knowledge.17Raiders in the Dark. A night sahuagin raid; Milo’s first kill; spiderweb and fish-head coins; a fog bank ahead.18The Chart and the Drift. The chart is burned and the compass fouled by an unknown saboteur. Quinn is found stowed away in the hold. Reza Sahil’s three contests (a drawn duel, Biscuit befriended, cards won); a replacement chart and the greatsword Marianne gained. Adrift.19The Wreck on the Sandbank. A planted lodestone removed from the compass. The coins lead to a drowned Waterdeep navy wreck; its dead crew fought. A ship’s log, a cap of water breathing, and Bran’s carvings found aboard. A kraken spawn surfaces.20The Dark Beacon. Escape from the kraken spawn. Crossing to dark Viledel; an allip destroyed.21Lighthouse Interiors. A dread wight and a dread wraith destroyed; the beacon relit. Quinn looks into the orb and is cursed. A keeper’s diary mentions the Tideworth.22Underway. Two days’ crossing from Viledel to Saltmere.
Saltmere

















































#Session23The Better Man. Docking in Saltmere (a blank permit gets them past the harbourmaster). Neve’s debt revealed. Errands at the market, chapel, forge, jeweller and healer. News of the new governor, Leon Thrace, and the old governor’s funeral; the party splits three ways.24A Tomorrow Worth Trusting. Odettia runs the funeral from the inside. Quinn and Milo infiltrate the manor and find a hidden dungeon with fifteen prisoners. Vander and Kaelith destroy the storehouse guardian.25**The Ones Who Never Left.** Escape to the Green Leaf; Luna’s mount form; four solo jobs around town; the Isolde vision, Cole’s cabinet, Harlan risen, Corv; Leon’s invitation.26**The Coven.** Familiars spot the coven; a fight in the woods at Harlan’s farm; Osric rescued; the lair beneath the farm; a guarded truce.27**The Governor’s Table.** Laura’s confession; Odettia’s bite; dinner with Leon and his offer; Quinn meets Isolde; the vial points beneath the manor.28**The Matter Is Closed.** Orders overheard; Milo’s mysterious father; Sibbet and Hobb examined; Osric found in a prisoner cart; a fight begins among the dungeon’s tendrils.29**Before First Light.** Fog and phoenix fire; eight prisoners escape and four die; Voss sounds the alarm; Osric rescued; Luna vanishes after Selûne’s rebuke; refuge at Harlan’s farmhouse.30**Until Midnight, I Am Yours.** Kaelith’s forearm vanishes; Osric wakes and tells his story; Isolde receives the letter and bracelet and releases Odettia’s bond; Milo tests the ward; the griffon answers, and a manor raid is planned.31**I Am Yours Until Midnight — Part 2.** The griffon raid takes Leon and the medic; Kaelith searches the manor; Quinn seeks help for his curse; Milo’s trap apparently kills Halflin and Luna returns; a warning goes wrong, and Quinn forms a blood bond with Isolde before the family meeting.32**I Am Yours Until Midnight — Part 3.** Isolde meets Leon, Corv vanishes, the party reunites at the caves and questions the medic. At midnight, the griffon departs and the oblex takes control.

sessions/session-25.title: Session 25: The Ones Who Never Left
sessions/session-25.content:
Played over two nights. Previous: Session 24 · Next: Session 26
Night one: a roof over their heads

The party slipped out of the storehouse ahead of a manor patrol and found rooms at the Green Leaf, run by the three-armed dwarf Gerta Wrack. Vander helped her shift crates and paid for the first night.
Gerta’s gossip included a foreign hunter who came to Saltmere decades ago, asked about the old ruling family, went up the manor road and never came back. He carried a mark stitched on his gear: two crossed lines through a closed eye, the same mark as in the book that taught Quinn his shadow technique.
Quinn laid out a theory: Leon as a vampire, explaining his lifelong illness and sudden recovery, the bloodless livestock, the vanished hunter and the shackled prisoners. He let slip that he grew up in a vampire household. Vander came round to the idea.
Pressed by Vander, Odettia insisted nothing about Leon felt cold or wrong. But she had seen his eyes flash crimson when they met.
Neve Saren delivered a letter to Odettia from her parents.
In the street outside the inn, Luna grew into a towering, glowing, saddled mount for the first time.

Night two: four jobs, one day

Each player played a solo scene while the others waited outside. The four met again at the Green Leaf at sunset.
Odettia at the Tailored Needle

The seamstress Henrietta hired Odettia to mend festival clothes. Odettia turned out to have a gift for needlework and added an embroidered border of vines and flowers to a shirt (“I can make a fortune on that”). Henrietta mentioned that Cole the harbourmaster had seen a griffin over the sea the day before; Odettia’s griffin token warmed.
An owl flew in, took a pair of old velvet gloves from a chest Henrietta never opens, and gave them to Odettia. At their touch, Aerdrie Faenya sent her a vision, and for the first time Odettia stayed on her feet. She was looking through the eyes of the gloves’ owner: in a torchlit dungeon, a woman with dark pinned hair and a grey dress lay dead, ice cold, with a wound across her chest.
Henrietta said the gloves belonged to Isolde, her partner of ten years, who vanished one morning twelve years ago. From Odettia’s description, Henrietta recognised the dead woman as the governess, the lady of the manor and Leon’s mother. Isolde had been her handmaiden. The governess died twelve years ago and the town was never told how; the old governor’s cruelty began almost to the day.
Odettia promised Henrietta she would find the truth.

Quinn at the docks

Working for Harbourmaster Edrik Cole, Quinn learned:

Prisoners have long gone through the dock to the dungeons under the manor, and the numbers have jumped: twelve in a single day.
A shipment of animals for Harlan’s farm “never arrived”.
Prison and torture equipment was signed for by the head of the Manor Guard.


He tasted a bottle of “wine” bound for Harlan’s farm. It was blood.
A drained body was pulled from the harbour, with two fang punctures below the elbow: the mark of a restrained, elegant vampire.
While Cole was busy, Quinn picked his private cabinet:

Brennick’s decades-old arrival record, with the closed-eye mark and “no departure recorded”
a mortality register showing bursts of deaths, and three this week (taken)
a governor’s standing order, renewed for about thirty years, letting manor wagons pass uninspected
a large payment to the ship Tideworth, marked “agent”
Cole’s own notes on the governess’s death: “horrible death”, “body mutilated”, circled “inside job?” (taken)



Vander at Harlan’s farm

Dead cows lay where they had stood, bloodless and untouched by scavengers. In the barn lay Harlan himself, with clean punctures in the crook of his elbow. He rose red-eyed and feral, and Vander cut him down with radiant steel.
Upstairs, Harlan’s wife Laura tested Vander by cutting herself and watching him. She told him a red-eyed, clawed woman had seized Harlan the night before, told Laura to get back inside if she wanted to live, and seemed not to mean her harm.
Vander buried Harlan under the oak, with his lantern at the head of the grave in the custom of his order.
On the ride back, fresh horse tracks led into the trees, and the symbol of the Order of Aster was carved into a trunk. Vander called out. A four-note whistle answered, one he feels he should know.

Kaelith at Yara’s apothecary

Kaelith made hangover cures (“Antivomix”) for Yara Dunwell and cured a feverish boy with marshmallow leaf after Yara’s tonic failed. The boy’s mother, Fenna, named her “Kaelith the Wise.” Near Yara’s preservation magic, Kaelith felt solid and anchored for the first time in this age.
A ragged, frost-rimed man came in: Corv, the traveller Yara once saved. When he and Kaelith touched hands, both their arms turned translucent to the bone. He was thrown five years forward by a broken dragon-blood time spell and has been fading ever since.
He gave Kaelith a nearly finished cure, missing one ingredient: “the thing that does not die, the thing that consumes”, which he has traced to the manor. The vial will react when it is close. The deal: if she completes it, he uses it and teaches her to make her own.

Back at the Green Leaf

The four pooled what they had learned. Odettia revealed that her ancestor Ilithrea Belabranta, the name Corv had mentioned, slew a green dragon.
Kaelith found that Laura was hiding bruises and healed them. Harlan had been beating her.
A rider in manor colours brought a letter from Leon Thrace:

Dinner tomorrow at dusk. “Come armed if it comforts you.”
He owes one of them a debt from his father’s funeral.
Two of his people are dead this week, he knows why, and he can’t say so publicly.


They accepted. Vander will go as Odettia’s guard.

sessions/session-26.title: Session 26: The Coven
sessions/session-26.content:
Working title. Previous: Session 25 · Next: Session 27

Owls at night. Odettia’s owl Ariane and Kaelith’s new owl Barry scouted the woods by Harlan’s farm overnight. They saw a lone traveller being stalked by pale women.
The clearing. Vander, keeping his promise to Laura, rode out with Kaelith, and the party followed. In a clearing, three young vampires were tearing at a bloodied man while an older woman watched.

Vander recognised the man as a knight of his own Order, charged in to protect him and healed him.
Kaelith raised a wall of wind to part the fighters; the vampires ignored it.
Quinn fought from the shadows with psychic strikes.
Odettia grappled the coven’s leader to stop the violence. The leader bit her neck, and Odettia resisted her charm.
Vander struck the leader, then held back and knocked her unconscious instead of killing her. The other vampires stopped.


Osric. The man was Osric, one of the seven knights who rode with Vander’s father Umber. Kaelith charmed him into telling the truth:

He tracked the Order of Aster key to Saltmere, and saw it around Leon Thrace’s neck at the funeral.
He saw Umber in Vander’s face.
He fears Sundar, who he says has turned to Shar and is hunting the rest of Umber’s company, blaming them for their father’s death.


The truce. The coven’s leader said Osric drew first blood. She said her coven hunts “a greater evil” in the manor that wears a familiar face in town, and that chaos in the manor “would not be frowned upon”. She left as mist.
The lair. Quinn found a hidden hatch in the farmhouse leading to a basement: hundreds of empty blood bottles, a tapestry of two crowned women (one resembling the murdered governess), and animal bones Kaelith judged to be one to ten years old.
Before they left:

Through his psychic link, Quinn arranged a private meeting with the coven leader behind the manor the next evening (a “hot date”). Vander thinks it’s unsafe.
Vander took a bag of gold from the farmhouse chest for Laura.
Osric took a room at the Green Leaf.

sessions/session-27.title: Session 27: The Governor's Table
sessions/session-27.content:
Previous: Session 26 · Next: Session 28
Before dinner


Quinn’s curse stirred, but he rolled a natural 20, boxed the intrusion up and set it aside for a while.


Osric had come to the Green Leaf an hour earlier, muttered “those bastards” and stormed back out.


Odettia’s bite. In the mirror: two closed punctures, cold skin, and fine black lines spreading along her veins. She isn’t turning yet, but if the lines pass the point she marked, symptoms begin. At the chapel the old priest said he can cure it on three conditions:

The vampire that bit her must be destroyed or willingly release her.
It must be done within three days at most.
He needs something tied to the attacker, ideally from where she rests.

Quinn followed her there, unseen.


Laura’s confession. Vander and Kaelith visited Laura, and Vander added 20 gold to her bag before she would talk. What she told them:

For twelve years a coven of frightened vampires has lived in her cellar. She sheltered them, fed them animals in secret, and made sure their weekly bottled blood arrived from the harbour, in carts bearing the governor’s symbol. Harlan never knew.
A few nights ago Harlan beat her. The coven came, and their leader, Isolde, asked, “Do you want me to take care of this?” Laura said yes.
Isolde said the last human she had wanted to kill was the old governor, twelve years ago.
The blood shipments stopped a week or two ago. Since then the coven has gone feral and hunts openly.

Laura is leaving the island. Luna gave her a parting blessing.


Dressing up. Odettia lent Kaelith a dark green velvet gown and conjured a red one for herself with her hat of disguise. Vander and Quinn went as they were. Milo came as Odettia’s ward, in a tuxedo borrowed from Gerta (no shoes).


The manor


Leon Thrace met them at the door: dark green coat, a chain around his neck vanishing under his shirt. His guards let them keep their weapons but warned that anyone who draws one dies. One guard is named Voss. Leon told them that cats have protected his house for generations, and stroked Luna.
The tour:

Portrait gallery. A pale gap between the old governor and Leon where his mother’s portrait hung. His father took it down soon after she died, more than ten years ago, when Leon was very young.
A nailed-shut door. The east-wing stair to the old dungeon, sealed by Leon after his father died, “for the better of the community”.
Rooftop conservatory and office. Moonflowers, his mother’s favourite, which he tends himself; Kaelith judged them flawlessly cared for. A lifelong illness kept him bedridden until the house medic brought a cure from overseas. His father died of illness after running himself into the ground. Odettia’s magical senses caught only faint threads of something dormant in him.


Leon’s philosophy. Pain should be acknowledged and put right, not memorialised. His father ruled by fear and was a softer man before Leon’s mother died.

Dinner


The table. A round table (“so we converse as equals”), six guards, a hundred-candle chandelier. Courses of broth, then sea bass, his mother’s favourite. Her name was Celandine.
Small details:

A guard mentioned a Gundwynd trader due in a few days.
Leon barely ate; he says his illness left him on a liquid diet. His glass was filled only from “his lordship’s cellar wine”. Quinn thought he smelled iron somewhere in the room.


Leon’s request. Seven townspeople killed in two weeks, drained of blood. One was the captain of the guard, three days ago. His guards would be “fodder”. On his first day as governor he sent a negotiator to the coven, and they sent back his head. He offered 800 gp (300 up front) to remove the coven. He also offered to tell the party what he knows about the Tideworth’s cargo if they help.
An eighth victim was reported during dinner. Later a guard announced they had trapped a vampire in a fortified building and shot her from the rafters. Odettia asked that the body be kept.
The party asked for a night to decide. Leon retired at eleven because of his “poor constitution”. When Quinn asked why he would kill his own kind, Leon said, “I’m sure I don’t know what you mean.”

Quinn’s errand

Slipping out unseen, Quinn found a quiet room with the same tapestry as in the farm cellar, this time with names stitched beneath: Celandine and Isolde. Along the hem: “Sister for sister, thread for thread, pull the name of the one not wed.” Pulling the thread of Isolde’s name opened a hidden pocket:

Celandine’s last letter to her sister: “He knows. Keep the boy safe if I can’t. Love, your sister.”
a travel bag with 100 gp and survival tools


In the orchard he met Isolde. “You walk quietly, little hunter… someone with fangs, I think.”

She wants a life with Henrietta, but the town hunts her every night.
“They killed my sister in front of me.” She holds everyone in the manor complicit.
She asked Quinn to open the orchard door to let her in. He refused.
She offered to release Odettia from the bite in exchange for Celandine’s letter. Quinn kept the letter for now.
When Quinn called Leon her nephew, she laughed: “You think that thing in there is my nephew?… That is the one question I would love the answer to.”
She will consult her coven, and warned that if Quinn crosses her, he’ll be the first she kills. He proposed meeting at Harlan’s farm at noon tomorrow; she didn’t answer.



Midnight

Odettia secretly cast Clairvoyance on Leon’s desk in the conservatory. What she saw or heard is still to come.
As the clock struck midnight, Kaelith’s hand turned translucent again. In her pack, Corv’s vial shook violently, its contents pooling downward, toward whatever lies beneath the manor.
Guards cut the evening short (a second vampire sighting in town) and saw everyone out. On the way, Voss mentioned rumours of a red-haired wanderer elsewhere in the Moonshaes.

In the carriage
The party argued it through:

Is Leon a vampire, something else entirely, or even an oblex?
Why did the coven only turn violent once the old governor died and the blood stopped?
Should they bring Leon and Isolde face to face?

Odettia would have felt it if the vampire that bit her had died, so the party assumes the one the guards killed wasn’t Isolde, but this was never confirmed. The likeliest plan is a return to the dungeons through the tunnel. Leon is still waiting for an answer.

sessions/session-28.title: Session 28: The Matter Is Closed
sessions/session-28.content:
Previous: Session 27
The orders behind the report
Odettia’s Clairvoyance caught a conversation in the manor office. A doctor said the dhampir’s blood had not clotted on a cloth; the other speaker ordered the sample kept. Odettia believed she was hearing Leon and his doctor, though the voices were not independently identified.
The conversation described a trap: a girl had taken a message into a shed, Voss had shut it behind her, and his men had killed her. The official account placed her beside her supposed victim. Orders followed to burn her body on the cliff before first light, with the arrows, without a crowd, and to stand the lanes down at three.
Milo’s father
Back at the Green Leaf, Vander’s healing gave the party a short rest. Milo sat unresponsive, silently moving his lips, surrounded by overwhelming magic.
Odettia tried Identify. She felt fear, grief and longing for family, then heard a distant voice: “This one’s mine.” She answered, “He is his own.” Her hand burned and she was thrown back. Milo woke confused and apologised for his “dad”. The party could not identify the presence.
Milo offered Odettia a drink he called a healing potion, stolen from a manor desk; it smelled of wine and did heal her. He also recalled two bodies on stone slabs, but could not retain the words of his experience. Exhausted and hungry, he stayed at the inn helping Gerta while the others investigated.
Sibbet and Hobb
At the guarded chapel, Kaelith became a ladybird and found a side medical room holding two bodies. Vander distracted guards with pirate rum while Quinn picked the rear lock and Odettia slipped inside.
A report named the dead woman Sibbet and the man Hobb. It alleged that Sibbet had stalked and drained Hobb before guards trapped her in a salt workshop and shot her through slits. A handwritten instruction called for Hobb’s body to be displayed as a warning about vampires.
Their examination challenged that account:

Hobb was human. His life force had been drained in a way unlike ordinary vampire feeding. The wounds on his neck were shallow, a knife lay on the slab, and dried, sulphurous residue coated his exposed skin.
Sibbet was a vampire the party recognised from the farm fight. Her mouth was clean of blood and residue. She bore the coven’s shared forearm tattoo.
Quinn remembered a chemical that could kill a vampire without a blow to the heart. Poisoned arrows and staged bite marks were the party’s explanation, not a confirmed finding.

Quinn took Sibbet’s metal, vine-like bracelet from her right wrist to show Isolde. The residue flakes were lost, not kept. The party closed and relocked the rear door.
The owls saw no activity on the cliffs. Ariane also showed Odettia a distant winged silhouette on the horizon; Odettia wondered if it was a griffon, but could not confirm it.
A prisoner transfer
The party returned to the cave entrance of the hidden passage. Quinn’s performance as a drunken intruder drew the guards’ attention, allowing the others through; he then escaped and climbed back into the tunnel.
Kaelith, still a ladybird, scouted an approaching cart. Two guards were transporting Osric, bound and gagged. Odettia disguised herself as a guard and presented Vander as another prisoner. Her bluff got him onto the cart beside Osric, with loose bonds he could escape. Kaelith rode underneath while Odettia and Quinn followed.
Beneath the manor
At about three in the morning, the cart reached the cells. About fifteen prisoners were connected to black, smoky tendrils that ran through cracks beneath a closed door at the corridor’s end. Kaelith thought of the Bearbarrow oblex, but these strands were more ethereal and less like ooze. What lay behind the door remained unknown.
When the guards tried to take Vander’s sword, he broke his bonds and attacked. Kaelith resumed her own form. The two escorts and two guards by the door fought them; Odettia and Quinn joined shortly afterwards.

Vander struck with Divine Smite, but a missed swing strained his right shoulder. He has disadvantage on Strength saving throws until the injury is treated; healing spells alone will not fix it.
Kaelith cast Spike Growth around the farther guards and used Land’s Aid to heal Vander. One prisoner could not remember his own name; another asked about his mother’s name.
Kaelith’s Produce Flame severed one prisoner’s tendril. Its detached end disintegrated, but the prisoner showed no immediate change.
Odettia’s Command made one guard flee for a turn; another resisted.
Crossbow bolts reduced Kaelith to 3 hit points and broke her concentration. Quinn landed a devastating psychic blade attack from hiding, then concealed himself again.
Vander reached Kaelith and restored 20 hit points with Lay on Hands, leaving her at 23.

Where play stopped
Combat is still underway. No guard was confirmed dead. Osric remains bound and gagged in the cart, and the prisoners remain in their cells. One tendril has been cut; the door is still unopened. Vander’s shoulder injury persists. The next round begins with Odettia.
Milo remains at the Green Leaf. Odettia’s bite is uncured, Quinn still holds Celandine’s letter and Sibbet’s bracelet, and no ingredient for Corv’s cure has been recovered. The order to burn Sibbet before dawn remains an urgent concern. See Open threads.
Continued in Session 29: Before First Light.

sessions/session-29.title: Session 29: Before First Light
sessions/session-29.content:
Previous: Session 28 · Next: Session 30
Fog and fire
The fight beneath Saltmere’s manor resumed with Osric bound and gagged in the cart. Odettia cast Fog Cloud, humming as mist poured from her hand and swallowed the corridor. The guards lost their bearings and fired blindly: one bolt wounded Osric, another struck a fellow guard, and a later shot narrowly missed Kaelith. [00:00:22–00:02:58; 00:17:25–00:19:39]
Kaelith cast Flaming Sphere to free the prisoners from the tendrils. With careful control she guided it through the bars, burning the strands without striking the captives. A prisoner remembered his daughter’s laughter; others recovered the sound of a wife’s voice and a father’s stories. The shrieks from beyond the closed door grew louder as more connections were severed. [00:06:44–00:14:24; 00:35:37–00:37:24; 00:56:20]
Vander charged into the fog. Selûne offered to be his eyes: his blade and eyes shone, and the fog lifted from his sight. He killed one guard. Quinn entered the mist and killed the other nearby guard with his psychic blades. Odettia’s imitation of a guard’s voice failed to obtain the cell keys, but her Healing Hands restored five hit points to Osric. [00:26:45–00:34:49; 00:41:36–00:45:06; 00:51:51–00:52:24]
Eight escaped, four died
Vander severed another strand with Sunbolt. Then the remaining tendrils changed: the wisps became solid, wrapped around four prisoners’ necks and killed them. Kaelith hurled her sphere at the withdrawing connection and cut it off; the detached material fell and writhed on the floor. [01:00:45–01:05:12]
The party opened the surviving captives’ cells. Quinn picked locks, Odettia melted three locks with phoenix-shaped fire, and Kaelith burned through the locks holding two elven twins. Vander guided a confused elderly man through the fog. Eight prisoners escaped; four died. [01:03:31–01:09:40; 01:20:43–01:21:40]
Odettia worried about who they were releasing. The elderly man’s remarks about his business partner troubled her, and a young woman tried to pick her pocket. She raised an illusory wall and questioned the prisoners, with Quinn coming to help. A frightened boy, Brennan, said he had been falsely accused of theft and brought there by boat. He appeared sincere, and Odettia sent her owl to guide him out. When the young pickpocket discovered the wall was an illusion, the others rushed through. [01:09:58–01:20:12]
The cart and the papers
Searching the dead guards, Vander found one key, thirty gold pieces and a charge sheet for Halflin, one of the elven twins. It listed numerous alleged offences and an extraction scheduled for that day. [01:22:46–01:25:25]
Odettia recognised the Gundwynd crest on Osric’s cart. It was a shipping container fitted with wheels and reinforced to hold something trying to escape; inside were bloodstains and scratches. A paper pinned to Osric listed alleged crimes including unlawful investigation and plucking a sunflower from the governor’s garden. The papers recorded accusations, not proof of every charge. [01:25:36–01:29:36]
Corv’s vial strained toward the reinforced door. The missing ingredient was still somewhere beyond their reach. [01:21:53–01:22:46]
Captain Voss’s warning
Luna healed Kaelith before the party approached the door. The guard’s key was too small. When Kaelith tried to burn through the door, ice crept from the other side and resisted her fire. A voice recognised as Captain Voss, captain of Leon’s guard, told them to take Osric and the prisoners and leave. Odettia challenged him; he invoked the governor’s authority and warned that their deaths would not be his responsibility. [01:31:34–01:37:05; 01:41:15–01:41:49]
Quinn discovered a fist-sized ventilation opening, climbed up and looked through. He reported four people and an unidentified mist beyond the door. Kaelith’s ritual detected a mage using ice magic there. What produced the tendrils remained unidentified. [01:43:05–01:45:29; 01:56:06–01:56:49; 02:09:27–02:09:32]
Voss rang an alarm and warned that the governor’s battalion would arrive in about two minutes. His warning, and his reluctance to kill them, seemed sincere. More bells answered from above. [01:57:19–02:00:57]
The forced retreat
Kaelith still wanted to reach the room and the remedy ingredient. As the others prepared to flee, Odettia struck her on the back of the head with her dagger’s handle, knocking her unconscious. Vander loaded Kaelith onto Luna beside Osric. Odettia used Celestial Revelation to fly. [02:01:04–02:02:16]
Odettia’s owl had seen the escaping prisoners reach an unguarded warehouse route. The party followed it and burst into the quiet harbour while alarms and torches spread around the manor above. They headed toward Harlan’s farm. Vander gave Brennan money for a room, and Odettia guided him to the Green Leaf, using her owl to alert Milo as well. Exhaustion caught up with everyone as dawn approached. [02:02:16–02:08:24]
A patrol stopped them on the road. Vander bluffed that they had been sent to seek support, and the guards let them pass. Quinn remained hidden and stole twenty gold pieces from one of them. [02:10:32–02:13:56]
Repent and make right
Outside town, Vander’s oath burned in his thoughts. He had freed people who prey on the weak. Selûne told him to repent and make things right, and Luna vanished, dropping Osric and Kaelith. Kaelith woke from the fall. Vander resolved to deal with the dangerous escapees after the party had rested; Halflin’s charge sheet remained in his possession. [02:15:10–02:21:36; 02:25:05–02:26:31]
Odettia examined the still-unconscious Osric and noticed sickly-sweet breath. Drugging or poisoning was suspected, not confirmed. She explained to Kaelith why she had forced the retreat, and Kaelith healed herself. [02:22:06–02:24:14]
Milo caught up and offered fifty gold from his tavern winnings. At the deserted farmhouse, Vander tried to imbue his greatsword with Selûne’s light, but it remained cold steel. His learned spells remained available; Luna and the Selûne-linked weapon blessing were lost. [02:26:39–02:30:38; 02:38:39–02:40:10]
Milo performed a fiery working and said he had set a hellish rebuke at the front door. Odettia left a warning to keep five feet away and a request to talk to the coven later. Milo marked the exclusion area in chalk. Quinn smelled blood toward the cellar but left it for after sleep. At about five in the morning, the party settled down. [02:31:10–02:37:03]
Where things stand

Osric is rescued but unconscious, with the cause of his condition unresolved.
Eight prisoners escaped and four died. Halflin, an elf and one of the twins, is among the escapees; Vander holds his sheet.
The reinforced door remains unopened. The mist, the mage’s identity, the tendrils’ source and Corv’s missing ingredient remain unresolved.
Saltmere is under alarm and lockdown. Another approach to the manor will be harder.
Vander needs to make amends and restore his bond with Luna and Selûne’s blessing; his shoulder injury also remains untreated.
The coven meeting, the blood scent in the cellar and the outcome of Sibbet’s before-dawn disposal order remain open. The party has settled to rest; a completed long rest has not yet been played.

sessions/session-30.title: Session 30: Until Midnight, I Am Yours
sessions/session-30.content:
Previous: Session 29 · Next: Session 31
The rest and the unraveling
The party rested at Harlan’s farmhouse, with the long rest expected to end around one in the afternoon. Vander played a sorrowful but determined tune on his pan flute. Odettia’s bite was worsening: black, web-like veins spread from the wound, her neck tightened and the promise of power clouded her thoughts. She counted two days remaining. Looking out after sleeping, she saw a thin plume of smoke along the cliff, but its source was not investigated. [00:00:06–00:05:27]
Kaelith’s left hand and forearm vanished up to the elbow. This time there was no translucent outline, and the limb did not return. She screamed. She could feel phantom movement, but could not make contact with the missing hand. [00:09:22–00:10:59; 00:15:08–00:15:39; 00:18:06–00:19:21; 00:24:25–00:24:33]
Odettia cast Identify and explained the result: Temporal Refuge, a spell cast by two people to bind someone in time, was unraveling. Its deterioration was tearing Kaelith’s body apart. It would not take her home. A taste of Corv’s unfinished remedy had no effect, and changing into a bear gave Kaelith only three legs. She still intended to finish the remedy for Corv first and learn how to make another; its final ingredient remained unrecovered. [00:11:01–00:11:12; 00:19:21–00:20:06; 00:21:38–00:25:17]
Quinn resisted another encroachment from the orb curse. Kaelith’s Pot of Awakening made a sound and developed cracks, but the shrub was not yet fully awakened. Milo asked his mysterious father about her missing arm and could offer no solution. [00:26:16–00:27:03; 00:33:01–00:36:32; 00:43:37–00:44:42]
Osric wakes
Odettia identified the sweet-smelling poison keeping Osric unconscious. Vander used Lay on Hands to remove it. Green vapour escaped Osric’s mouth, and he woke nauseated and asking for water. Vander went to the well. The magic worked, but he described it as hollow without his familiar connection to Selûne. Luna and his weapon blessing remained absent, and resting had not cured his shoulder injury. [00:18:21–00:18:32; 00:36:47–00:40:20]
Later, Osric explained his capture. Guards had seized a companion from their woodland camp; he remembered a hippogriff-like crest on their shoulders. When he demanded justice, they chained him, put him in the cart and sent him down the tunnel. He said the other knight was now dead. Osric offered to fight alongside them if armed. Vander lent him his trident, which Osric accidentally sent through the open window; Odettia recovered it on her return. [01:19:42–01:24:56; 01:36:36–01:36:48]
A bracelet and a broken peace
Quinn and Odettia met Isolde beneath a shaded tree near the farm. Quinn approached first with Sibbet’s bracelet. Isolde said a message from Voss had promised peace at a warehouse. She sent Sibbet, who never returned. Quinn described finding her on the chapel slab and gave Isolde the bracelet. She called it a kindness she would not forget, addressing him as brother. [00:48:20–00:55:39]
Isolde still described vampirism as a gift and saw potential in Odettia to lead a coven. She said Celandine had turned first: working as a night courier, her sister challenged a rogue vampire feeding on someone and was attacked. Later, Celandine offered Isolde the change. [00:55:42–00:59:34]
When Quinn and Odettia described their suspicion of poison, Isolde named Lily of the Shade, a white flower used to make poison that harms vampires. She said the governor’s greenhouse held the only specimen nearby. It was a new lead into Sibbet’s death, rather than proof of who poisoned her. [01:00:07–01:02:11; 01:43:07–01:43:30]
Celandine, Leon and the old governor
In exchange for a promise to arrange a meeting with Leon, Isolde answered their questions. She said Leon was born with vampiric blood that his body could not tolerate. Blood replacement, surgery and injections failed, leaving him ill for most of his life. Then his father died and Leon suddenly recovered. She now smells sulphur on him and doubts he is her nephew. The party explained oblexes to her; she had not known the creature by that name. Her suspicion does not settle what has happened to Leon. [01:03:00–01:07:40]
Isolde said Celandine was already a vampire when she married the old governor. He arranged their life around nighttime and secretly supplied prisoners for her to feed on. After years of failed treatments, Celandine wanted to take Leon elsewhere for care. According to Isolde, the governor discovered her plan and flew into a rage; Isolde found her sister staked on the dungeon floor, with guards behind her. Isolde holds the old governor responsible for Celandine’s death. [01:11:39–01:13:51; 01:17:33]
Quinn gave Isolde Celandine’s last letter. She wept as she read, her eyes lingering on “keep the boy safe.” After Odettia offered sympathy, Isolde touched her bitten neck and willingly released her bond. She told Odettia to find a priest for cleansing. The release was complete; the cure was not. Odettia still needed an item tied to Isolde and the Father’s rite, and intended to retrieve the gloves from Henrietta. [01:14:15–01:16:57; 02:03:55–02:04:24]
Isolde also identified the old governor as the payer of twelve years’ weekly blood shipments. She could understand a grieving father but could not forgive her sister’s killer. Asked whether she would fight if Leon had been taken over, she answered that she wanted to protect the true version of her nephew. She expected the promised meeting at dusk, at the farm, then left to join the mourning coven. [01:16:59–01:19:42]
Osric’s account of Umber and Sundar
At the farmhouse, Vander and Kaelith heard Osric’s account of Umber’s death. Masked attackers in blue cloaks bearing gold WSS letters ambushed the company. An arrow struck Umber in the neck; the survivors pursued his killers and their numbers dwindled. [01:24:56–01:28:22]
The key was returned to the Order by a member of the company before the later theft from the reliquary. Osric’s account made that sequence clear. [01:28:22–01:29:24]
Osric recalled records found while following the killers: the key suppressed an oblex’s ability to produce copies. This was his account of the records, rather than an effect the party had tested. [01:30:38–01:32:30]
He said Sundar entered a temple of Shar while pursuing the WSS. Years later, when they crossed paths again, Sundar bore a dark aura and shot one of their remaining companions through the skull. The others fled. Vander wondered whether this was still his brother; the explanation remained uncertain. [01:32:35–01:36:27]
Milo tests the door
When Quinn and Odettia returned, Milo tested his own ward by throwing a pebble at the front door. An enormous explosion blew away the door and frame and left the porch sagging. Milo stood soot-covered, his hair swept back. Kaelith used Elementalism to pour water over the fire, and Odettia cleaned him with magic. The farmhouse entrance was wrecked. [01:36:36–01:40:03]
The griffon’s answer
As the party considered how to reach Leon and the dungeon, Odettia felt the Griffontack grow warm. She went outside and called. A griffon descended: the same creature that had touched her amulet at the watchtower in the Fields of the Dead. She approached, bowed and touched it, feeling an immediate connection. Its help was temporary, discussed as lasting until midnight: a partnership with a willing creature. [01:44:00–01:48:36; 01:59:35–01:59:54; 02:04:40–02:04:51]
The plan took shape: Odettia and Kaelith would fly to the manor, try to seize Leon from the greenhouse or balcony and bring him to Isolde. Kaelith wanted to remain behind as a ladybird to seek the missing ingredient, with the others following by land toward town and the cave route. Communication and the exact approach were still being discussed. [01:49:10–01:55:23; 01:55:56–01:59:35]
Odettia mounted the griffon and pulled Kaelith up. Play paused as the raid was about to begin. The raid, abduction and dungeon return had not yet been carried out. [01:55:00–01:55:56]
Where things stand

Kaelith’s left forearm is missing, and the final ingredient for Corv’s remedy remains unrecovered.
Odettia has Isolde’s willing release, but still needs the cleansing rite and an item tied to her.
Osric is awake and the poison is removed. His testimony links Umber’s killers to the WSS and suggests a purpose for the key.
Isolde holds the letter and bracelet and expects a meeting with Leon at dusk.
The griffon has answered Odettia. She and Kaelith are mounted for the planned manor raid; the others intend to approach by land.
Halflin remains at large; Luna and the weapon blessing remain lost. Vander’s shoulder still needs treatment.
The farmhouse entrance is wrecked. The cellar blood scent, the cliff smoke and Sibbet’s final fate remain uninvestigated.

sessions/session-31.title: Session 31: I Am Yours Until Midnight — Part 2
sessions/session-31.content:
Previous: Session 30. Next: Session 32. Evidence times use P1, P2 and P3 for the session’s three recordings; each part starts its own clock. Scenes switch between separated groups.
No link, and a parting signal
Quinn tried to extend his psychic link to cover the distance from the farm to the manor, but the attempt failed. The separated groups would have to manage without it. Vander fired an unusually impressive Sunbolt into the sky and felt a familiar, long-unheard presence humming at the edge of his mind. He wondered about his old Lathander training, but received no explanation. [P1 00:00:57–00:04:37; 00:10:37–00:11:44]
Vander, Osric and Milo set off by land. Quinn initially stayed behind. Odettia and Kaelith flew toward the manor on the watchtower griffon, disguising its riders with an illusion of sky. The griffon itself was still visible. [P1 00:12:04–00:15:43]
Ice through the greenhouse
Kaelith called Barry back from the cliff, sharing her distress and gratitude. Odettia sent Ariane ahead, then landed in a tree near the manor to scout through her familiar’s eyes. Guards noticed the perched griffon. Ariane saw Leon at his desk with the medic who had treated Quinn: a hand rested on Leon’s back, and magic flowed from the medic into him. [P1 00:18:35–00:22:56; 00:25:35–00:28:49; 00:32:10–00:32:56]
Odettia cast cold Dragon’s Breath on the griffon, its magic taking the shape of tiny icy pixies. It froze the glass, then crashed through the greenhouse roof. Leon and the medic turned amid the falling shards. Odettia used Suggestion to prevent the medic using magic against her or her allies, and the griffon seized both men. The spell replaced her concentration on Dragon’s Breath. [P1 00:35:08–00:44:40; spell clarified P2 00:28:24–00:31:37]
Kaelith leapt from the griffon, burned the greenhouse’s Lily of the Shade plants with Produce Flame and changed into a ladybird. Leon cried that those were all he had. The shattered greenhouse was left behind as Odettia prepared to escape with the captives. [P1 00:44:45–00:47:49]
A noble, his companions and a hooded guide
Vander hid his armour and red hair under a hood, asking Milo to call him “Uncle K.” Milo acquired a cloak for himself and an unexpectedly elegant disguise for Osric: pinstripe suit, top hat and monocle. Osric would pose as a noble leading bounty hunters into the guarded town. [P1 00:48:43–00:56:27]
Vander recruited a hooded rapier-wielder calling herself Julianne. After Osric talked and bribed their way through the checkpoint, she sold Vander a lead: Halflin might be found at the rope works by the docks after sundown. She accepted five gold for the information, in addition to the two he had given for joining them, while keeping her face concealed. As she left, she told him to give Halflin a message: his sister said hello. [P1 00:57:38–01:08:48]
The rope works looked deserted. Across the docks, four guards watched the separate warehouse containing the dungeon entrance. Vander and Osric decided to enter the rope works as prospective customers. [P1 01:10:43–01:12:31]
Quinn seeks help for the orb curse
Quinn crossed the wall by climbing a tree and visited Yara Dunwell. He described the headaches and the presence that returned more strongly each time he resisted it. He had not yet suffered gaps in his memory. [P2 00:00:07–00:01:50; 00:03:00–00:08:37]
Yara believed the curse threatened to separate spirit from body, leaving a spirit and an undead form if it overcame him. She could not remove it: he would need someone versed in soul magic, probably in a larger settlement. Her warning described what might happen, not a transformation already suffered. [P2 00:08:54–00:12:30]
She gave him an experimental three-dose mixture using herbs and preservation magic. A dose would help his next attempt to resist the orb within twenty-four hours, but would not cure it. She asked him to report what happened. Quinn also paid fifty gold for Poison of Silence, enough to coat about five arrows and interfere with a target’s magic; its detailed effects remained unexplored. [P2 00:12:44–00:20:51]
His attempt to recover money by picking a noble’s pocket went badly. A bodyguard caught and burned his wrist. Quinn tumbled free, failed to intimidate the man, and left for the meeting point. [P2 00:22:30–00:28:22]
Kaelith’s search
Inside the greenhouse, Corv’s vial was completely dormant. Kaelith searched anyway. A ledger listed unfamiliar names, dates spanning five years and tally marks under “cuttings.” In Leon’s study she saw a signed receipt from two weeks earlier for a “live specimen” and an “accompanying specialist.” Neither document explained what the terms meant. [P2 00:31:49–00:36:55; 00:39:28–00:41:35]
In the medical wing she found an undated observation chart for L. Thrace. Daytime entries described normal energy and bodily readings. The 12:30 a.m. entry read “agitated,” “violent,” “new powers?” Beyond it lay the familiar shackled bed and bloodstained floor. A partially patched opening still let her reach the hidden stair. [P2 00:43:00–00:48:48]
Kaelith passed at least thirty guards and new checkpoints underground as alarms began to sound. The cells had been scrubbed clean: no prisoners, smoke or severed tendrils remained. The door that had resisted the party was now ajar. [P2 00:50:10–00:52:13]
Beyond it stood two worn restraint chairs beneath open pipes, with bloodstains and thick residue on the stones. One person took notes while another cleaned with magic. They discussed an incoming transfer in two days, reviewing roughly ten or eleven prisoners and their alleged crimes with routine administrative detachment. They did not explain what would be done to them. [P2 00:54:35–00:58:47]
This was the room the vial had previously drawn her toward, but whatever it had reacted to was absent. Following sulphur-smelling residue through the pipes, Kaelith emerged into Leon’s ornate bedroom, then returned down the same route. She had found evidence and a connection between the rooms, but no ingredient and no answer to her failing spell. [P2 00:58:47–01:03:56]
Leon at the farm
Odettia distracted the guards with an illusory gelatinous cube and flew away. Three crossbow bolts missed. She descended into the trees and returned to Harlan’s farm, where Quinn rejoined her. Leon was set down; the griffon kept the suggested medic pinned. [P2 01:06:03–01:13:32]
Odettia told Leon that Isolde was his aunt and that his father had killed Celandine. Leon, overwhelmed, said his mother had died of sickness and denied knowing an aunt. In the cellar, Odettia illuminated the tapestry. He recognised his mother and her handmaiden, but did not accept their resemblance as proof of sisterhood. [P2 01:14:18–01:21:24]
Leon admitted that he already knew his mother was a vampire and that he was half-vampire. He still disputed the account of her murder. Asked how he had recovered, he said that they had found a cure. When Odettia named the oblex, he showed recognition but challenged why the cure’s nature mattered. He did not explain it. [P2 01:21:33–01:23:55]
He also mentioned seeing a man resembling Vander in town a couple of weeks earlier. Odettia suggested his brother, but that identification was not confirmed. After hearing about Celandine’s letter, Leon agreed to talk to Isolde in the hope of peace, even while doubting their kinship. [P2 01:20:17–01:20:54; 01:24:37–01:27:05]
Thunder at the rope works
When Vander’s scene resumed, his Sunbolt had knocked Halflin from the rafters. Vander tried to knock him unconscious, but Halflin scrambled away. Vander chased him through the rope works. Halflin protested that Vander would put him in chains after seeing what “that thing” had done to him. Vander offered the villagers’ judgement, then threatened chains or death. Halflin ran for the rear exit. [P2 01:27:14–01:32:08]
An enormous explosion destroyed the rear of the building. A voice told Vander “all has been restored,” and Luna returned, brushing against his leg. From beyond the wreckage, Milo explained that he had placed a trap after his “dad” suggested adding a little more power. He believed Halflin was dead; the fugitive’s body was not examined before they fled. [P2 01:32:08–01:34:38]
Vander gathered Osric, Milo came round to the front, and they escaped through a nearby pub. Three warehouse guards went to investigate the blast. The party tried to slip through the alleys, but Vander’s armour betrayed them and the guards gave chase. They stayed together, outpaced the pursuit and reached the Green Leaf, where Gerta hid them in a locked back room. [P2 01:34:47–01:37:26; P3 00:00:14–00:07:07]
The warning that went wrong
Kaelith emerged from the dungeon through the warehouse. A replacement orb-form guardian was waiting there, and additional carts bore the Gundwynd crest. She spotted Vander’s fleeing group, followed them to the Green Leaf and changed back inside the refuge. Luna’s return brought her first smile of the day, but the lost ingredient left her despairing. Milo asked his father for help and received none. [P3 00:07:19–00:13:44]
Through Barry, Kaelith saw about a hundred armed soldiers, some with magic, searching in the direction the griffon had flown. They did not know the farm’s precise location. She tried to warn Odettia and Quinn away from the dungeon and alert them to the danger. [P3 00:13:55–00:16:16; 00:24:34–00:25:19]
Barry found Ariane, but the urgent message became only “dungeon, urgent.” Odettia took it to mean their friends were in danger underground. Barry’s increasing panic made the misunderstanding worse. Odettia sent Ariane to check the surroundings while Quinn went to meet Isolde. No rescue journey had begun. [P3 00:25:19–00:27:58; 00:29:54–00:33:37]
Blood and a promise
At sunset Isolde arrived with about twelve members of her coven, explaining that she had prepared for an uncertain meeting. Quinn told her Leon was there, and she acknowledged the party had kept its agreement. [P3 00:31:11–00:32:43; 00:34:59–00:35:30]
Calling Quinn a true ally, Isolde bit her hand and offered a pact to look out for one another. Quinn reciprocated. Their blood mingled as they shook hands, and he felt a bond form. Isolde promised that she and her coven would be there if he needed them. [P3 00:35:43–00:37:10]
Quinn and Isolde walked toward Leon. Play paused immediately before their conversation. [P3 00:37:10–00:37:23]
Where things stand

At the farm: Odettia, Quinn, Leon, the medic and the griffon; Isolde and her coven have arrived. The family meeting is about to begin.
At the Green Leaf: Kaelith, Vander, Milo, Osric and the returned Luna, sheltered in Gerta’s back room.
The search force is moving toward the farm’s region. Its arrival and the party’s response have not happened.
Luna and Vander’s blessing are restored. Halflin is apparently dead after Milo’s trap; the other escapees remain unresolved.
Kaelith’s forearm remains missing, the vial dormant and the ingredient unrecovered. The manor records and pipes are new leads.
Quinn has temporary help for the orb curse and Poison of Silence, neither used during this session, and a new bond of mutual aid with Isolde.
Odettia still needs cleansing. Leon’s cure remains unexplained, and no peace settlement has been reached.

sessions/session-32.title: Session 32: I Am Yours Until Midnight — Part 3
sessions/session-32.content:
Previous: Session 31. Times refer to the Session 32 recording.
What Leon owed Saltmere
Quinn brought Isolde to meet Leon at Harlan’s farm. She named herself his aunt and told him that his father had murdered Celandine for trying to take him away for treatment. Leon had grown up believing she died of illness. He said his own recovery came after something from Baldur’s Gate was injected into him, and that it had side effects. Asked if he was the creature Odettia had tracked to the island, he answered, “I am, and I am not.” [00:08:25–00:19:09]
Leon wanted to tell Saltmere his story and put the matter to its people. Odettia challenged his defence of feeding on prisoners. Leon said they had been sentenced to die and defended the arrangement as a cost he had accepted. Odettia doubted that all the prisoners were guilty and rejected his justification.
